| SF32LB581VCN36 | BGA256 | 1 MB boot NOR Flash + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM on MPI1 |
| SF32LB583VCC36 | BGA256 | 1 MB boot NOR Flash + 2 × 8 MB OPI-PSRAM on MPI1 and MPI2 |
| SF32LB585V5E56 | BGA256 | 4 MB boot NOR Flash + 4 MB NOR Flash on MPI1 + 32 MB HPI-PSRAM on MPI2 |
| SF32LB586VDD36 | BGA256 | 1 MB boot NOR Flash + 2 × 16 MB HPI-PSRAM on MPI1 and MPI2 |
| SF32LB587VEE56 | BGA256 | 4 MB boot NOR Flash + 2 × 32 MB HPI-PSRAM on MPI1 and MPI2 |

</div>

When selecting a variant, check these items first:

- Required framebuffer, asset, audio, and model-memory size
- Display interface and target resolution
- External storage and Wi-Fi interface requirements
- PCB manufacturing capability for BGA256, 0.4mm-pitch HDI layout

## Integration Path

Use this sequence to turn an SF32LB58x shortlist into a validated design:

1. **Prove the firmware path.** Start with the [SiFli SDK getting-started guide](../../getting-started/sifli/getting-started-sifli-sdk.md), then use the [SiFli SDK workflow](../../develop/platforms/sifli-sdk/overview.md) and [examples](../../develop/examples/index.md) to validate the display, graphics, audio, storage, and Bluetooth configuration.
2. **Choose the integration vehicle.** Evaluate [SF32LB58-MOD](../modules/SF32LB58-MOD.md) when reducing RF, BGA, and memory-layout risk is valuable, or use [SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD](../devkits/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD.md) for early board-level validation.
3. **Design and review the hardware.** Use the local [hardware design guide](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_hardware_design_guide.md) — including its [schematic](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_schematic_checklist.md) and [PCB layout](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_pcb_layout_checklist.md) checklists — before releasing the schematic or layout. Validate the BGA256 HDI and memory-routing assumptions early.
4. **Verify the authoritative source.** Confirm the exact orderable part and package against the SiFli [datasheet], [user manual], [Original Design Guide (wiki.sifli.com)], and [Hardware Application Note (GitHub source)].

<!-- uf-faq:start -->
## Frequently Asked Questions

**What are the key specifications of SF32LB58x?**
SF32LB58x pairs an application CPU (2× Cortex-M33 @240 MHz) with a low-power core (Cortex-M33 @48/96 MHz, a user-programmable core), 3.7 MB of internal SRAM and dual-mode Bluetooth (BT Classic + BLE). Graphics: ePicasso 2.0 + Vivante GCNanoUltraV (vector). Package: BGA256 (8.5 × 6.5 mm). USB 2.0 HS. Family-level values; verify the exact part number's datasheet.

**Which display interfaces does SF32LB58x support?**
SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / EPD / JDI / RGB / MIPI. Availability varies by part number and package.

**How much in-package memory does SF32LB58x offer?**
Up to 32 MB + 32 MB of in-package PSRAM and up to 8 MB of in-package NOR Flash, depending on the part number.

**What supply voltage does SF32LB58x need?**
1.71–3.63 V, depending on the variant. Confirm the exact range in the datasheet.

**Where do I start a hardware design with SF32LB58x?**
Start with the [SF32LB58x hardware design guide](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB58x_hardware_design_guide.md) for schematic, power, clock/RF and PCB layout guidance, then use the schematic and layout checklists before releasing the board.
<!-- uf-faq:end -->

## Related Products

### Module

[SF32LB58-MOD](../modules/SF32LB58-MOD.md) packages the SF32LB586VDD36 chip, its RF matching network, and in-package HPI-PSRAM plus storage options into a ready-to-integrate module. Use it when the project needs 58-series capability but should reduce RF, BGA, and memory-layout risk early in hardware development.

### Development Kits

[SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD](../devkits/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD.md) is the starting point for power-tree, display, storage, audio, RF, USB, and SDIO design decisions.

### Reference Products

Typical SF32LB58x end products include premium watch platforms, high-resolution wearable HMIs, smart dashboards, portable connected terminals, and devices that combine Bluetooth, display, audio, storage, and local AI workloads.

---

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3/

Summary: SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3: compact SF32LB52x evaluation board with a jumper-selectable 1.8 V or 3.3 V MCU supply and direct GPIO, display, audio, USB access.

# SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3

## Overview

The SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 is a compact development board for direct evaluation of SF32LB52x chips. A board jumper selects a 1.8 V or 3.3 V supply for the MCU. Main MCU signals are exposed through edge headers, and the castellated through-holes accept pin headers without soldering. The board suits engineers who need direct access to GPIO, serial buses, display signals, audio, ADC, PWM, and power rails.

At 30.88 mm × 68 mm, the board is compact for bench prototypes while providing practical interfaces for SF32LB52x hardware and firmware bring-up.

![SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 front view](assets/sf32lb52x/Core-3p3_Front_look.png){ width="50%" loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 — Front View</em></div>

![SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 back view](assets/sf32lb52x/Core-3p3_Back_look.png){ width="50%" loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 — Back View</em></div>

## Board Variants

<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 Board Variants</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Variant | MCU | In-Package Memory | On-Board Memory |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-N1 | SF32LB52BU36 | 1 MB SPI NOR Flash | None |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-N4 | SF32LB52BU56 | 4 MB SPI NOR Flash | None |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-R4N16 | SF32LB52EUB6 | 4 MB OPI-PSRAM | 16 MB SPI NOR Flash |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-R8N16 | SF32LB52GUC6 | 8 MB OPI-PSRAM | 16 MB SPI NOR Flash |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-R16N16 | SF32LB52JUD6 | 16 MB OPI-PSRAM | 16 MB SPI NOR Flash |

</div>

Use the NOR-only variants for compact Bluetooth, control, and simple HMI work. Use the PSRAM + external NOR variants when the application needs larger graphics assets, frame buffers, file systems, or application storage.

**Source discrepancy — verify the board label before selection:** SiFli's [detailed Core-3p3 board guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3.html) calls the SF32LB52JUD6 configuration `R16N16 V1.0.0` (current), while its [development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html) lists the same JUD6 / 16 MB PSRAM / 16 MB NOR configuration as `N16R16`. The detailed guide's revision-information line says EUB6 has 8 MB of co-packaged PSRAM, but its feature list and variant table say 4 MB. SiFli's [SF32LB52 overview](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-Wiki/blob/main/source/en/hardware/SF32LB52/SF32LB52-Overview-B3.md) also specifies 4 MB for EUB6, so this article uses 4 MB. Confirm the board marking and matching schematic/BOM when the exact board suffix matters.

## Board Highlights

- SF32LB52x MCU variants with NOR-only or PSRAM + NOR configurations
- 48 MHz main crystal and 32.768 kHz RTC crystal
- USB Type-C power and USB-to-UART download/debug through CH340N
- Onboard PCBA antenna and I-PEX antenna connector
- Jumper-selectable 1.8 V or 3.3 V supply for the MCU
- USB 2.0 FS signals routed to the edge header
- 37 GPIOs exposed; the MCU provides 3 UARTs, 4 I2C interfaces, 2 GPTIMs, 2 SPI interfaces, and 6 GPADC channels
- All GPIOs can be configured as UART, I2C, or GPTIM; pin multiplexing also includes SPI, PWM, I2S, PDM, and wake inputs
- 16-pin, 0.5 mm-pitch FPC display connector; display interfaces include SPI, DSPI, and Quad-SPI, with DDR-mode QSPI support
- I2C touch-panel signals
- Analog microphone and differential audio output pins
- One user LED
- Power key and function key
- Test points for single-rail current measurement; SiFli also documents single-MCU, minimum-system, and whole-board power tests

## When to Use This Board

Choose SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 when you need the most direct access to SF32LB52x signals.

- Bring up custom daughterboards or sensor boards
- Evaluate SF32LB52x memory variants
- Prototype LCD, audio, USB, and GPIO functions
- Measure current on individual power rails
- Validate firmware before designing a compact product PCB

For a smaller castellated module-style board, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano](SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano.md). For a ready display board with audio amplifier, TF-card slot, and battery charger, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD](SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD.md).

## Power

The board supports three power inputs:

- USB Type-C power, recommended for normal development and debugging
- 5 V input through the edge header's 5 V and GND pins when USB is disconnected
- 3.3 V input through the edge header's 3.3 V and GND pins when USB is disconnected; an external bench supply may be used

A separate board jumper selects the MCU supply between 1.8 V and 3.3 V. This setting is distinct from the external 1.8 V and 3.3 V header power pins; check the pinout and the schematic for the matching board revision before changing the jumper or powering external circuitry.

For single-rail current measurements, place an ammeter in series with the rail under test at the board's measurement points.

When USB Type-C is connected, the board can also provide 3.3 V, 1.8 V, and 5 V outputs through selected header pins. Confirm the required direction before connecting external circuits.

The board includes a power switch. The CH340N RTS# signal can control board enable, allowing the host tool to reset the MCU during download or debug workflows.

## Download and Debug

Use the USB Type-C UART port for firmware download and software debug.

- **Download mode**: enable BOOT in the download tool, then power or reset the board.
- **Debug/log mode**: disable BOOT, then power or reset the board.
- **Reset**: use the on-board reset/power-key function or the tool-controlled RTS reset path.

## User Controls

<div align="center"><em>User Control Signals</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Function | GPIO | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| LED | PA32 | Active high |
| KEY1 | PA34 | Active high, supports 10s long-press reset |
| KEY2 | PA33 | Active high |

</div>

## Display Interface

The board supports SPI, DSPI, and Quad-SPI LCD interfaces, including DDR-mode QSPI, through a vertical 16-pin FPC connector with 0.5 mm pitch, a flip-up latch, and bottom contacts. It carries LCD reset, backlight PWM, TE, chip select, clock, four data lines, and I2C touch signals.

![FPC adapter cable](assets/sf32lb52x/FPC-22P.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>FPC Adapter Cable</em></div>

### 16-Pin LCD FPC Signal Map

<div align="center"><em>16-Pin LCD FPC Signal Map</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | GND | Ground |
| 2 | PA00 | LCD reset |
| 3 | PA01 | Backlight PWM |
| 4 | PA02 | LCD TE / I2S1_MCLK |
| 5 | PA03 | LCD CS / I2S1_SDO |
| 6 | PA04 | LCD CLK / I2S1_SDI |
| 7 | PA05 | LCD D0 / I2S1_BCK |
| 8 | PA06 | LCD D1 / I2S1_LRCK |
| 9 | PA07 | LCD D2 / PDM1_CLK |
| 10 | PA08 | LCD D3 / PDM1_DAT |
| 11 | 3.3V | Display power output |
| 12 | GND | Ground |
| 13 | PA09 | Touch interrupt |
| 14 | PA11 | Touch I2C SDA |
| 15 | PA20 | Touch I2C SCL |
| 16 | PA10 | Touch reset |

</div>

SiFli's Chinese board guide says the 1.85-inch AMOLED module connects directly through a 16-pin FPC cable. Its English guide instead specifies an FPC-22p cable, and the illustration filename is `FPC-22P`. The board connector itself is 16-pin. The sources do not resolve this mismatch; verify the cable pin count and pin mapping against the display module before connecting it.

## Header Signal Summary

The board exposes two 24-pin edge headers. The first side focuses on general GPIO, SPI2, USB, GPADC, and power. The second side focuses on LCD, touch, debug UART, audio, and power.

![SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 pinout](assets/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3-T-pinout.svg){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3 Pinout</em></div>

### General I/O Header

<div align="center"><em>General I/O Header Pin Assignments</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin Range | Signals | Main Functions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2-9 | PA44..PA37 | UART, I2C, GPTIM, SPI2, wake inputs |
| 10-11 | PA36 / PA35 | USB DM / USB DP, UART, I2C, GPTIM |
| 12-15 | PA31..PA28 | GPADC3..0, SPI1, I2S1, UART, I2C |
| 17 | 3.3V | 3.3V input or output depending on USB power |
| 18-21 | PA27..PA24 | Wake inputs, SPI1, I2S1 |
| 22 | PA34 | UART, I2C, GPTIM, GPADC6, WKUP10 |
| 23-24 | PA33 / PA32 | UART, I2C, GPTIM, GPADC5 / GPADC4 |

</div>

### LCD, Audio, and Debug Header

<div align="center"><em>LCD, Audio, and Debug Header Pin Assignments</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin Range | Signals | Main Functions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2-11 | PA00..PA09 | LCD, touch, PDM, I2S, UART, I2C |
| 12-15 | MIC_ADC, MIC_BIAS, DACP, DACN | Analog microphone and audio output |
| 17 | 1.8V | 1.8V input or output depending on USB power |
| 18-20 | PA10, PA11, PA20 | PA10: CTP_RST; PA11: CTP_SDA; PA20: CTP_SCL; all support UART, I2C, and GPTIM |
| 21 | PA21 | UART, I2C, GPTIM |
| 22-23 | PA18 / PA19 | UART0 RX/TX, SWDIO/SWCLK, download/debug |
| 24 | 5V | 5V input or output depending on USB power |

</div>

## External Flash and SDIO Pins

Some variants include an external 16 MB QSPI-NOR Flash. The shared storage/SDIO pin group is:

<div align="center"><em>External Flash and SDIO Pin Group</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| MCU GPIO | Shared Flash / SDIO Function |
| :--- | :--- |
| PA12 | MPI2_CS / SD1_D2 |
| PA13 | MPI2_D1 / SD1_D3 |
| PA14 | MPI2_D2 / SD1_CLK |
| PA15 | MPI2_D0 / SD1_CMD |
| PA16 | MPI2_CLK / SD1_D0 |
| PA17 | MPI2_D3 / SD1_D1 |

</div>

Check whether these pins are already occupied by the mounted Flash before using them for SDIO or other expansion functions.

## Audio Expansion

The board routes analog microphone bias/input and differential DAC output. The microphone and a Class-AB/D amplifier for driving a speaker are external; select them for the intended audio path.

## SDK Build Targets

The SiFli SDK build configuration uses the following exact board-target names with `scons --board=<board_name>`:

- `sf32lb52-core_n4`
- `sf32lb52-core_n16r16`

These are SDK build-target identifiers, not necessarily the product names printed on a board or module. The [Supported Boards index](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/supported_boards/index.html) and the SDK's [`build_config_gcc.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-SDK/blob/main/build_config_gcc.yaml) may enumerate different sets; confirm the target against the SDK revision in use.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD/

Summary: SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD: display-focused SF32LB52x board for fast bring-up of SPI, QSPI, and MCU/8080 displays with touch, audio, storage, and battery support.

# SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD

## Overview

The SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD is a display-focused development board for the SF32LB52x family. It is built around an SF32LB52x module and is intended for rapid development of products that use SPI, DSPI, QSPI, or MCU/8080 display interfaces.

The board combines the MCU module, display connectors, touch interface, analog microphone input, analog audio output, USB-C, USB-to-UART debug, TF-card storage, and battery support on one evaluation platform. It is a practical starting point for smartwatch-style HMIs, compact dashboards, display peripherals, and other SF32LB52x applications that need a screen early in development.

![SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD front view](assets/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52x-DevKit-LCD_Front_Look.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD — Front View</em></div>

![SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD back view](assets/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52x_DevKit-LCD_Back_Look.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD — Back View</em></div>

![SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD block diagram](assets/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52x_DevKit-LCD_Block_Diagram.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD — Block Diagram</em></div>

## Board Highlights

- SF32LB52x module platform, compatible with SF32LB52-MOD-1, SF32LB52-MOD-A, and SF32LB52-MOD-B
- QSPI/SPI/DSPI LCD support through a 22-pin FPC connector
- 8-bit MCU/8080 LCD support through the FPC and 40-pin expansion header
- I2C touch-panel support
- USB-C for USB-to-UART download/debug and board power
- Separate USB-C interface for USB2.0 FS use cases
- On-board MEMS microphone and Class-D audio power amplifier
- MicroSD card slot using SPI
- Battery connector and ETA9640P linear charger
- 40-pin expansion header for display, GPIO, storage, audio, and power signals

## When to Use This Board

Choose SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD when the project needs a ready display platform instead of a minimal breakout board.

- Bring up QSPI, SPI, DSPI, or MCU/8080 LCD panels
- Validate touch-panel integration
- Test LVGL or custom UI applications on SF32LB52x
- Evaluate microphone input and speaker output
- Prototype TF-card storage
- Compare module options before committing to a custom PCB

For a smaller board with castellated edges, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano](SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano.md). For maximum pin breakout and direct signal access, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3](SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3.md).

## Hardware Configuration

<div align="center"><em>Hardware Configuration Summary</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Area | Configuration |
| :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD-1-N16R8 | SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8 / SF32LB525UC6; 16MB QSPI-NOR + 8MB OPI-PSRAM |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD-1-A128R16 | SF32LB52-MOD-1-A128R16 / SF32LB527UD6; 128MB QSPI-NAND + 16MB OPI-PSRAM |
| Clocks | 48MHz main crystal and 32.768kHz RTC crystal on the module |
| RF | On-board antenna or IPEX connector selected by 0-ohm resistor |
| Display | QSPI/SPI/DSPI and 8-bit MCU/8080 |
| Touch | I2C touch interface |
| Audio | MEMS microphone input and Class-D speaker amplifier |
| Storage | MicroSD card slot over SPI |
| USB | USB-to-UART Type-C and USB2.0 FS Type-C |
| Battery | Single-cell Li-ion/Li-poly battery connector |
| Charger | ETA9640P linear charger, default 450mA charge current |

</div>

The board codes and memory configurations above follow SiFli's [development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html). Before using a board as a design baseline, check its revision against the board marking and the matching design package.

The A128R16 Flash labels differ across the official sources: the [OpenSiFli module-model guide](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-Wiki/blob/main/source/en/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.md) identifies the module as 128 MB SPI-NAND, while the board-model guide lists the corresponding DevKit SKU as 128 MB QSPI-NAND. The sources do not explain whether this reflects the fitted part or interface wording. Confirm the Flash part and bus mode against the schematic/BOM for the exact board revision before relying on this configuration.

## Getting Started

### Required Hardware

- SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD board
- LCD module compatible with the selected interface
- USB 2.0 data cable, Type-A to Type-C or equivalent
- Host computer running Windows, Linux, or macOS

### Optional Hardware

- Speaker
- TF card
- Single-cell Li-ion/Li-poly battery, typically 450mAh to 500mAh
- Second USB cable when UART debug and native USB testing are needed at the same time

### Basic Setup

1. Connect the LCD module to the correct LCD connector.
2. Connect the USB-to-UART Type-C port to the host computer.
3. Open SifliTrace or the SiFli firmware download tool.
4. Select the detected serial port.
5. Power the board and download or run the target firmware.
6. After the display lights, verify touch, graphics, storage, and audio functions as required by the application.

Use a real data-capable USB cable. Charge-only cables can power the board but will not expose the serial or USB data interface.

## Power

SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD can be powered in two main ways:

- USB Type-C power from either USB connector
- Battery power through the on-board battery connector

For firmware download and normal debugging, use the USB-to-UART Type-C port. Battery power is useful when testing untethered display, audio, and low-power behavior.

The board integrates an ETA9640P linear charger. The maximum supported charge current is 1A, and the default constant-current setting is 450mA. Use a single-cell Li-ion or Li-poly battery and verify connector polarity against the board silkscreen before connecting the battery.

## Download and Debug

The USB-to-UART port is the primary firmware download and log interface.

- **Download mode**: enable the BOOT option in the download tool, then power or reset the board.
- **Debug/log mode**: disable the BOOT option, then power or reset the board to enter normal serial-log operation.

Some SF32LB52x boards use the USB-to-UART RTS signal for reset. If the board resets unexpectedly when the serial port is first opened, disable modem or hardware flow control in the host serial-port settings.

![Disable modem flow control in serial-port advanced settings](assets/sf32lb52x/Modem.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>Disabling Modem Flow Control in Serial-Port Settings</em></div>

## LCD and Touch Interface

The board supports QSPI LCD panels through a 22-pin, 0.5mm-pitch FPC connector. The connector is a vertical, flip-lock style connector. If a panel uses a different pin order, use an adapter board before connecting it.

Supported LCD and touch capabilities include:

- SPI, DSPI, and QSPI LCD signaling
- DDR-mode QSPI LCD signaling
- 8-bit MCU/8080 LCD signaling
- LCD reset, chip select, clock, data, TE, and backlight PWM
- I2C touch-panel SDA/SCL, interrupt, and reset

The original SiFli board note lists `TFT-H043A28WQISTKN22_V0-3` as a supported display model.

### 22-Pin QSPI FPC Signal Map

<div align="center"><em>22-Pin QSPI FPC Signal Map</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | LEDK | LCD backlight cathode |
| 2 | LEDA | LCD backlight anode |
| 3 | PA07 | MCU8080 DB0 / QSPI D2 |
| 4 | PA08 | MCU8080 DB1 / QSPI D3 |
| 5 | PA37 | MCU8080 DB2 |
| 6 | PA39 | MCU8080 DB3 |
| 7 | PA40 | MCU8080 DB4 |
| 8 | PA41 | MCU8080 DB5 |
| 9 | PA42 | MCU8080 DB6 |
| 10 | PA43 | MCU8080 DB7 |
| 11 | PA02 | MCU8080 TE / QSPI TE |
| 12 | PA00 | LCD reset |
| 13 | PA04 | MCU8080 WR / QSPI CLK / SPI CLK |
| 14 | PA05 | MCU8080 RD / QSPI D0 / SPI SDI |
| 15 | PA03 | MCU8080 CS / QSPI CS / SPI CS |
| 16 | PA06 | MCU8080 DC / QSPI D1 / SPI DC |
| 17 | VDD_3V3 | 3.3V output |
| 18 | PA31 | Touch interrupt |
| 19 | PA33 | Touch I2C SDA |
| 20 | PA30 | Touch I2C SCL |
| 21 | PA09 | Touch reset |
| 22 | GND | Ground |

</div>

**Source pin-count discrepancy — verify before connecting a display:** SiFli labels the connector and signal table as 22-pin, but its accompanying connection drawing numbers contacts 1 through 24 and marks pins 22–24 as GND. The source does not reconcile the mismatch. Check the physical connector and schematic for the exact board revision before selecting or wiring a flex cable; do not assume a 22-pin cable fits a 24-position connector.

## Key Module Pin Assignments

![SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD 40-pin header definition](assets/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52x_DevKit-40p-define.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>40-Pin Header Definition</em></div>

<div align="center"><em>Key Module Pin Assignments</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Module Pin | Signal | Board Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PA44 | VBUS_DET | Charger insertion detection |
| PA43..PA37 | DB7..DB2 | MCU/8080 LCD data |
| PA08..PA07 | DB1..DB0 / QSPI D3..D2 | LCD data |
| PA06 | DC / QSPI D1 | LCD data/command |
| PA05 | RD / QSPI D0 | LCD data |
| PA04 | WR / QSPI CLK | LCD clock |
| PA03 | CS / QSPI CS | LCD chip select |
| PA02 | TE / QSPI TE | LCD tearing-effect signal |
| PA01 | BL_PWM | Backlight control |
| PA00 | RSTB | LCD reset |
| PA33 / PA30 | I2C SDA / SCL | Touch panel |
| PA31 / PA09 | Touch INT / RST | Touch panel |
| PA24, PA25, PA28, PA29 | SPI1 | TF-card interface |
| PA26 | Card detect / LED | Shared function |
| PA20 / PA27 | UART RX/TX | User UART |
| PA18 / PA19 | Debug UART RX/TX | Download and software debug |
| PA10 | AU_PA_EN | Audio amplifier enable |
| MIC_ADC_IN / MIC_BIAS | Analog microphone | Microphone input |
| AU_DAC1P_OUT / AU_DAC1N_OUT | Analog audio | Speaker amplifier input |

</div>

## Module Compatibility Notes

- SF32LB52-MOD-1 uses pin 17 as a 3.3V output that is disabled by default and must be enabled in software.
- SF32LB52-MOD-A/B use pin 17 as a 3.3V power input.
- SF32LB52-MOD-1 uses pin 27 as a 3.2V to 4.7V VBAT input.
- SF32LB52-MOD-A/B use pin 27 as a 3.3V power input.
- On SF32LB52-MOD-1, the VBAT power-on threshold is 3.58V and the power-off threshold is 3.48V. For non-battery supply testing, 3.8V is recommended on VBAT.
- PA21 on module pin 62 is only available on SF32LB52-MOD-A/B. It is not connected on SF32LB52-MOD-1.
- Module pins 62 to 68 may be connected internally to NOR Flash by default. To use SDIO externally, select a module variant without internal Flash on those pins.

## Audio

The board includes a MEMS microphone and an audio power amplifier.

- Use the on-board microphone path for analog audio input validation.
- Use the speaker connector for audio output testing.
- The external speaker path supports up to 3W into 4ohm according to the original board note.

## Storage

The MicroSD socket is connected over SPI. It is suitable for validating file systems, image assets, logs, and data recording before moving to a custom board.

## SDK Build Targets

The SiFli SDK uses the following exact board-target names with `scons --board=<board_name>`:

- `sf32lb52-lcd_52d`
- `sf32lb52-lcd_n16r8`
- `sf32lb52-lcd_a128r16`

These are SDK build-target identifiers, not necessarily the product names printed on a board or module. The [Supported Boards index](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/supported_boards/index.html) and the SDK's [`build_config_gcc.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-SDK/blob/main/build_config_gcc.yaml) may enumerate different sets; confirm the target against the SDK revision in use.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano/

Summary: SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano: compact castellated SF32LB52x development board for product-like prototypes, small display bring-up, and solder-down evaluation.

# SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano

## Overview

The SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano is a small SF32LB52x development board for compact prototypes and embedded evaluation. It uses castellated half-holes around the board edge, making it suitable both as a stand-alone development board and as a solder-down module in early product prototypes.

The board measures 51mm × 20.32mm and exposes the key SF32LB52x resources needed for GPIO, UART, I2C, SPI, LCD, I2S, GPADC, PWM, USB, and analog audio development.

![SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano front view](assets/sf32lb52x/Nano_Front_look.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano — Front View</em></div>

![SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano back view](assets/sf32lb52x/Nano_Back_look.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano — Back View</em></div>

## Board Variants

<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano Board Variants</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Variant | MCU | In-Package Memory | External Flash |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano-N4 | SF32LB52BU56 | 4MB SPI NOR Flash | None |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano-N16R16 | SF32LB52JUD6 | 16MB OPI-PSRAM | 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano-A128R16 | SF32LB52JUD6 | 16MB OPI-PSRAM | 128MB QSPI-NAND Flash |

</div>

The N4 variant is suitable for compact control, Bluetooth, and simple UI applications. N16R16 pairs 16 MB OPI-PSRAM with 16 MB QSPI-NOR, while A128R16 pairs 16 MB OPI-PSRAM with 128 MB QSPI-NAND. Both suit applications that need larger display assets, external file systems, or a frame buffer or working memory in PSRAM.

**Source discrepancy — verify before selection:** SiFli's [detailed Nano board guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/sf32lb52x/SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano.html) calls its 16 MB OPI-PSRAM + 16 MB NOR configuration `R16N16 V1.0.0`; the [current development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html) lists the same memory configuration as `N16R16` and separately lists `A128R16` with 16 MB OPI-PSRAM + 128 MB QSPI-NAND. The detailed guide does not describe A128R16 specifically. For that SKU, rely on the model-guide listing rather than transferring details from the N16R16 board description. Before choosing firmware or a storage layout, verify the board marking and the current schematic/BOM.

The SiFli sources also differ slightly on the Nano board dimensions: the detailed guide gives 21 × 51 mm, while the model guide specifies 51 × 20.32 mm. The 51 mm side agrees, but the shorter dimension differs by 0.68 mm. This page uses the more precise model-guide value; verify the mechanical drawing for the exact board revision before enclosure or carrier-board design.

## Board Highlights

- 51 mm × 20.32 mm compact board
- Castellated half-hole edge layout for solder-down prototypes
- USB Type-C power and USB-to-UART download/debug through CH340N
- GPIO, UART, I2C, SPI, GPADC, PWM, I2S, PDM, and wake-capable pins exposed
- QSPI LCD support through a 16-pin FPC path, typically using a 22-pin-to-16-pin adapter cable
- I2C touch-panel support
- Analog microphone input and differential audio output pins
- USB2.0 FS routed to edge pins
- Two user LEDs
- Power key and function key

## When to Use This Board

Choose SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano when the prototype should stay close to a final product form factor.

- Build compact Bluetooth and display prototypes
- Solder the board onto a carrier PCB
- Test product-like pin assignments before custom board design
- Compare NOR-only, QSPI-NOR, and QSPI-NAND configurations with PSRAM
- Bring up LCD, audio, sensor, and USB functions in a small footprint

For easier bench wiring and wider signal breakout, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3](SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3.md). For a display-rich board with charger, TF card, microphone, and speaker amplifier, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD](SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD.md).

## Power

The board supports three power approaches:

- USB Type-C power, recommended for development
- 3.3V input through the 3.3V and GND castellated pins when USB is not connected
- 5V input through the 5V and GND castellated pins when USB is not connected

When USB Type-C is connected, selected 3.3V and 5V pins can be used as outputs. Verify power direction before attaching external circuits.

The board includes a power switch controlled through the CH340N RTS# signal, allowing tool-controlled reset behavior.

## Download and Debug

Use the USB Type-C UART interface for firmware download and serial logs.

- **Download mode**: enable BOOT in the download tool, then power or reset the board.
- **Debug/log mode**: disable BOOT, then power or reset the board.
- **RTS reset behavior**: if opening the serial port unexpectedly resets or powers down the board, disable modem or hardware flow control in the host serial-port settings.

![Disable modem flow control in serial-port advanced settings](assets/sf32lb52x/Modem.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>Disabling Modem Flow Control in Serial-Port Settings</em></div>

## User Controls

<div align="center"><em>User Control Signals</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Function | GPIO | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| LED1 | PA31 | Active low |
| LED2 | PA32 | Active low |
| KEY1 | PA34 | Active high, supports 10s long-press reset |
| KEY2 | PA33 | Active high |

</div>

## Castellated Pin Summary

The Nano board exposes two edge pin groups. The first group carries audio, SPI1, debug UART, USB-adjacent power, and GPADC-capable pins. The second group carries SPI2, USB FS, wake-capable GPIOs, and power.

### Front-Side Edge Signals

| Pin | Signal | Main Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 2 | DACP | Analog audio output |
| 3 | DACN | Analog audio output |
| 4 | MIC_ADC | Analog microphone input |
| 5 | MIC_BIAS | Microphone bias |
| 6 | PA30 | I2S1_LRCK / GPADC2 / UART / I2C |
| 7 | GND | Ground |
| 8 | PA19 | UART0_TXD / SWCLK / debug |
| 9 | PA18 | UART0_RXD / SWDIO / debug |
| 10 | PA29 | SPI1_CS / I2S1_BCK / GPADC1 |
| 11 | PA28 | SPI1_CLK / I2S1_SDI / GPADC0 |
| 12 | PA25 | SPI1_DI / I2S1_SDO / WKUP1 |
| 13 | 3.3V | 3.3V input/output |
| 14 | GND | Ground |
| 15 | PA24 | SPI1_DIO / I2S1_MCLK / WKUP0 |
| 16 | 5V | 5V input/output |

</div>

## LCD Interface

The board supports QSPI LCD panels through a 16-pin FPC signal set. The original board note describes connection to the Huangshan Pi 1.85-inch AMOLED screen through a 22-pin-to-16-pin FPC cable.

![22-pin to 16-pin FPC adapter cable](assets/sf32lb52x/22p-to-16p.png){ loading="lazy" }

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | GND | Ground |
| 2 | PA00 | LCD reset |
| 3 | PA01 | Backlight PWM |
| 4 | PA02 | LCD TE / I2S1_MCLK |
| 5 | PA03 | LCD CS / I2S1_SDO |
| 6 | PA04 | LCD CLK / I2S1_SDI |
| 7 | PA05 | LCD D0 / I2S1_BCK |
| 8 | PA06 | LCD D1 / I2S1_LRCK |
| 9 | PA07 | LCD D2 / PDM1_CLK |
| 10 | PA08 | LCD D3 / PDM1_DAT |
| 11 | 3.3V | Display power output |
| 12 | GND | Ground |
| 13 | PA09 | Touch interrupt |
| 14 | PA11 | Touch I2C SDA |
| 15 | PA20 | Touch I2C SCL |
| 16 | PA10 | Touch reset |

</div>

## External Flash and SDIO Pins

The N16R16 variant includes external 16MB QSPI-NOR Flash. The storage pin group is:

<div align="center"><em>External Flash and SDIO Pin Group</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| MCU GPIO | Shared Flash / SDIO Function |
| :--- | :--- |
| PA12 | MPI2_CS / SD1_D2 |
| PA13 | MPI2_D1 / SD1_D3 |
| PA14 | MPI2_D2 / SD1_CLK |
| PA15 | MPI2_D0 / SD1_CMD |
| PA16 | MPI2_CLK / SD1_D0 |
| PA17 | MPI2_D3 / SD1_D1 |

</div>

These pins may be occupied by the mounted Flash depending on the variant. Check the exact board assembly before using them as expansion pins.

## Audio Expansion

The Nano board exposes analog microphone input, microphone bias, and differential analog audio output. Add an external microphone circuit and audio power amplifier as required by the target product.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP/

Summary: SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP: wearable-oriented SF32LB52x board with AMOLED, touch, sensors, audio, battery charging, and current measurement for low-power evaluation.

# SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP

## Overview

The SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP is also known as **立创黄山派**, **LCKFB-HSPI-SF32LB52-ULP**, and **SF32LB52-ULP**. It is a compact ultra-low-power wearable development board built around the SF32LB52x family, positioned as a smartwatch and fitness-band prototype platform rather than a simple MCU breakout board.

Compared with the LCD, Nano, and Core-3p3 boards, this board is more product-like: it combines an SF32LB52 module, AMOLED display, touch, microphone, speaker amplifier, RGB LED, vibration motor drive, motion sensor, magnetic sensor, ambient-light sensor, battery charging, and power-measurement jumpers. That makes it especially useful when the product question is not just "does the MCU run?" but "how does the whole wearable system behave on battery?"

SiFli's [ULP board guide][Original SiFli Wiki Article] remains a placeholder. For the detailed board configuration, use SiFli's Chinese [Huangshan Pi development-board guide][Original SiFli Huangshan Pi Guide], which documents board V1.0.0; its component values below are the baseline for that revision. The separate [LCKFB hardware wiki] does not identify its board revision and lists several different component numbers. Treat those as a possible revision/source mismatch, not interchangeable parts, and verify the actual board markings, schematic, and BOM before design work.

**Release-status caveat:** SiFli's V1.0.0 guide says the documented board was then for internal trial and would be revised before external release. This statement is specific to that source revision; it does not establish the status or BOM of later boards. Verify the exact board revision and BOM.

The [SiFli SDK board page][SiFli SDK ULP Board Page] lists this board target as `sf32lb52-lchspi-ulp`. The SDK board page and the package-contents section of the Chinese Huangshan Pi guide use `SF32LB52X-MOD-1-N16R8`, while the SiFli [module model guide][SiFli Module Model Guide] and the GPIO-table caption use `SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8`. The sources do not explain this `X` difference. The SDK target is clear; verify the fitted module's marking and BOM rather than inferring that the two SKU spellings identify different hardware.

![SF32LB52-ULP wearable board assembly reference](assets/sf32lb52x/52-ULP-1p85-install.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-ULP — Wearable Board Assembly Reference</em></div>

![Huangshan Pi SF32LB52 block diagram](assets/sf32lb52x/HSP_Block_Diagram.svg){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>Huangshan Pi SF32LB52 — Block Diagram</em></div>

## Naming

<div align="center"><em>Board Naming Aliases</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Name | Where It Is Used |
| :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP | SiFli/OpenSiFli board-family naming |
| SF32LB52-ULP | Short hardware/product name |
| LCKFB-HSPI-SF32LB52-ULP | LCKFB project/order naming |
| 立创黄山派 / 立创・黄山派 SF32LB52 | Chinese product and documentation name |

</div>

Use these names as aliases for the same board family when searching for hardware documents, examples, purchase pages, or community material. For schematic, pinout, or BOM work, always confirm the exact board revision and vendor document set.

## Board Highlights

- SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8 module based on SF32LB52x
- SF32LB525UC6 standard module configuration
- 8MB OPI-PSRAM, 144MHz interface
- 128Mb QSPI-NOR Flash, 72MHz STR mode
- 48MHz main crystal and 32.768kHz RTC crystal
- On-board PCBA antenna
- 1.85-inch AMOLED display, 390 x 450 resolution
- Quad-SPI display interface with touch support
- On-board MEMS microphone
- Analog audio output with Class-D speaker amplifier
- External speaker connector for 3W/4ohm or 2W/8ohm speakers
- USB Type-C UART interface through CH340N for download, debug, and power
- USB2.0 FS signals exposed through the 30-pin expansion connector
- MicroSD card slot using SPI
- One function key and one power/reset key
- SK6812MINI-HS RGB LED (SiFli Huangshan Pi V1.0.0 guide; the unversioned LCKFB page lists WS2812B-2020)
- Vibration motor driver circuit with external motor solder pads
- LSM6DS3TR-C 6-axis IMU
- MMC5603NJ 3-axis magnetic sensor
- LTR-303ALS-01 ambient-light sensor
- Battery charger and power-management devices for wearable power testing
- 2x15-pin, 1.27mm-pitch expansion header with GPIO and current-measurement support

## When to Use This Board

Choose SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP / 立创黄山派 when the goal is wearable system validation.

- Build watch, band, and sensor-rich wearable prototypes
- Evaluate AMOLED UI behavior on the SF32LB52x platform
- Test touch, motion sensing, magnetic sensing, ambient-light sensing, audio, vibration, and RGB LED behavior together
- Measure battery, system, and 3.3V current paths during sleep and active use
- Validate wake-up flows driven by buttons, sensors, touch, or firmware timers
- Compare real product-like power behavior against early estimates from simpler DevKit boards

For a display-focused general evaluation board, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD](SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD.md). For compact solder-down module prototyping, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano](SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano.md). For maximum direct pin access during early bench bring-up, use [SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3](SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3.md).

## Hardware Configuration

<div align="center"><em>Hardware Configuration Summary</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Area | Configuration |
| :--- | :--- |
| Core module | SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8 |
| MCU | SF32LB525UC6 |
| PSRAM | 8MB OPI-PSRAM, 144MHz interface |
| Flash | 128Mb QSPI-NOR Flash, 72MHz STR mode |
| Display | 1.85-inch AMOLED (ZC-A1D85W-010), 390 x 450, 800 cd/m², Quad-SPI |
| Display driver | CO5300AF-01 |
| Display power IC | BV6802W |
| Touch controller | FT6146-M00 |
| Microphone | On-board MEMS microphone |
| Speaker output | Class-D amplifier, external GH-1.25mm speaker connector |
| Storage | MicroSD card over SPI |
| Motion sensor | LSM6DS3TR-C 6-axis IMU |
| Magnetic sensor | MMC5603NJ 3-axis magnetometer |
| Ambient-light sensor | LTR-303ALS-01 |
| USB-UART | CH340N over USB Type-C |
| Battery | External Li-ion battery through GH1.25mm connector |
| Charger | SY6103, maximum charge voltage 4.5 V; default 450 mA constant-current setting; maximum current 500 mA |
| Protection/power devices | SY5320 OVP, LP5240HVF load switch, ETA5055V330DS2F LDO |

</div>

**Revision-dependent component list — verify before design:** SiFli's V1.0.0 [Huangshan Pi guide][Original SiFli Huangshan Pi Guide] lists SY6103 charger, SY5320 OVP, and SK6812MINI-HS RGB LED. The unversioned [LCKFB hardware wiki] instead lists AW32001ECSR in its feature list and AW23001ECSR in its charging section, plus LP5305AQVF OVP and WS2812B-2020 RGB LED. The sources do not establish whether these differences reflect a hardware revision or stale documentation. Use the SiFli V1.0.0 values only for that documented baseline; verify the actual board markings, schematic, and BOM before relying on component-specific behavior.

## Package Contents

The Huangshan Pi board set is documented as including:

- Core board
- Screen board
- Battery
- Speaker

Verify the purchased kit contents before planning a lab setup, because accessory bundles may differ by seller or production batch.

## Power and Battery

The board supports two primary power modes:

- USB Type-C power
- Standalone battery power

The battery input is intended for a single-cell Li-ion battery using a GH1.25mm connector with forward pin order. The documented charging configuration supports a maximum charge current of 500mA, with a default constant-current setting of 450mA.

When using the board without a battery and supplying VBAT from a bench supply, the documented VBAT input range is 3.7V to 4.7V, with 3.8V recommended for normal-voltage supply testing. The SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8 power thresholds are documented as 3.58V for power-on and 3.48V for power-off.

The LCKFB hardware guide warns that the long-press key function may not work when no battery is connected. Verify this behavior on the exact board revision and intended power setup.

## Power Measurement Jumpers

The board exposes current-measurement jumpers for the major power paths.

<div align="center"><em>Power Measurement Jumper Assignments</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pins | Path | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5-6 | VBAT path | Insert a current meter between battery/charger and downstream system |
| 7-8 | VSYS path | Insert a current meter in the VSYS path |
| 11-12 | VCC_3V3 path | Insert a current meter in the 3.3V main rail |

</div>

For normal operation, pins 5-6, 7-8, and 11-12 must be shorted with jumpers. Remove the appropriate jumper only when inserting a current meter or power analyzer.

## Download and Debug

Use the USB Type-C UART interface for firmware download, serial logs, and board power during normal development.

Required hardware for first bring-up:

- SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP / 立创黄山派 board
- USB 2.0 data cable
- Host computer running Windows, Linux, or macOS

Optional hardware:

- External speaker
- TF card
- Li-ion battery, 450mAh or larger
- Second USB cable when UART debug and native USB testing are needed at the same time

Use a real data-capable USB cable. Charge-only cables can power the board but will not expose the serial data interface.

## SDK Build Targets

SiFli's SDK uses the exact board-target name `sf32lb52-lchspi-ulp` with `scons --board=<board_name>`. This is an SDK build-target identifier, not necessarily the product name printed on a board or module. Confirm the target against the [Supported Boards index](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/supported_boards/index.html) and the SDK's [`build_config_gcc.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-SDK/blob/main/build_config_gcc.yaml) for the SDK revision in use.

## Key Signal Assignments

<div align="center"><em>Key Signal Assignments</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Signal | Function |
| :--- | :--- |
| PA44 | VBUS_DET, charger insertion detect |
| PA43 | KEY2 |
| PA42 | Audio_PA_EN |
| PA41 | Touch interrupt |
| PA40 / PA39 | Sensor I2C1 SCL / SDA, per the GPIO-assignment table; see the header-pin discrepancy below |
| PA38 | VSYS to VSYS_1 switch control |
| PA37 / PA33 | Touch I2C SCL / SDA |
| PA36 / PA35 | USB DM / DP |
| PA34 | HOME key and 10s long-press reset |
| PA32 | RGB LED data |
| PA31 | Sensor interrupt 1 |
| PA30 | VSYS_1 to HR3V3 switch control |
| PA27 | SD-card detect |
| PA24, PA25, PA28, PA29 | SPI1 MicroSD interface |
| PA20 | Vibration motor PWM |
| PA19 / PA18 | Debug UART TXD / RXD |
| PA11 / PA10 | Charger I2C0 SDA / SCL |
| MIC_BIAS / MIC_ADC_IN | Microphone bias and input |
| AU_DAC1P_OUT / AU_DAC1N_OUT | Analog audio output |
| PA08..PA03, PA02, PA01, PA00 | QSPI display, TE, backlight PWM, and reset |
| PA15..PA12, PA16, PA17 | MPI2 / SD1 signals, internally used by module Flash on the N16R8 module |

</div>

## 30-Pin Expansion Header

The 30-pin header exposes power, USB, sensor, display-adjacent, storage, vibration, debug, key, and charger-control signals.

<div align="center"><em>30-Pin Expansion Header Signal Map</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin Group | Signals | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1-2 | USB_VBUS_5V | 5V from USB when connected; can be 5V input when USB is not connected |
| 3-4 | GND | Ground |
| 5-6 | VBAT_S / VBAT | Short for normal operation; open for VBAT current measurement |
| 7-8 | VSYS_S / VSYS | Short for normal operation; open for VSYS current measurement |
| 9-10 | GND | Ground |
| 11-12 | VCC_3V3_S / VCC_3V3 | Short for normal operation; open for 3.3V current measurement |
| 13 / 15 | PA36 / PA35 | USB DM / DP |
| 14 / 16 | PB39 / PA40 | SiFli's V1.0.0 header table labels these Sensor I2C1 SDA / SCL; pin 14 conflicts with the GPIO-assignment table (see below) |
| 17 | PA32 | RGB LED data, also usable as GPIO |
| 18 | PA30 | Sensor power control; GPIO use may affect PA39/PA40 behavior |
| 19-23 | PA29, PA24, PA28, PA25, PA27 | SPI1/SD-card related pins; expansion use conflicts with the on-board TF card |
| 24 | PA20 | Vibration PWM; expansion use conflicts with motor drive |
| 25 / 27 | PA19 / PA18 | Debug UART TXD / RXD |
| 26 / 28 | PA34 / PA43 | Power/reset key and function key |
| 29 / 30 | PA11 / PA10 | Charger I2C0 SDA / SCL |

</div>

**Source pinout discrepancy — verify before wiring:** SiFli's V1.0.0 GPIO-assignment table maps sensor I2C1_SDA to PA39, while its 30-pin header table identifies header pin 14 as PB39 and labels it I2C1_SDA; pin 16 is listed as PA40/I2C1_SCL. The LCKFB tables repeat the PA39/PB39 difference but do not state a board revision or reconcile the entries. Treat the MCU pad/route for header pin 14 as unresolved: check the schematic/BOM for the exact board and verify continuity before connecting a peripheral. Do not assume PA39 and PB39 are interchangeable.

## Display and Touch Interface

The board uses an AMOLED display path and exposes a 22-pin QSPI FPC signal set. SiFli's V1.0.0 table marks pins 5-10 as NC; the table below includes all 22 positions and identifies those pins explicitly.

<div align="center"><em>22-Pin QSPI Display and Touch FPC Signal Map</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | VBAT | Display-side VBAT output |
| 2 | PA01 | Backlight PWM for TFT-style use |
| 3 | PA07 | QSPI D2 |
| 4 | PA08 | QSPI D3 |
| 5 | NC | Not connected |
| 6 | NC | Not connected |
| 7 | NC | Not connected |
| 8 | NC | Not connected |
| 9 | NC | Not connected |
| 10 | NC | Not connected |
| 11 | PA02 | QSPI TE |
| 12 | PA00 | LCD reset |
| 13 | PA04 | QSPI/SPI clock |
| 14 | PB05 (SiFli V1.0.0 FPC table) | QSPI D0 / SPI SDI; the separate GPIO-assignment table lists PA05 |
| 15 | PA03 | QSPI/SPI chip select |
| 16 | PA06 | QSPI D1 / SPI DC |
| 17 | VDD_3V3 | 3.3V output |
| 18 | PA41 | Touch interrupt |
| 19 | PA33 | Touch I2C SDA |
| 20 | PA37 | Touch I2C SCL |
| 21 | PA09 | Touch reset |
| 22 | GND | Ground |

</div>

**Source pinout discrepancy — verify before connecting a display:** SiFli's V1.0.0 22-pin FPC table assigns PB05 to connector pin 14 for QSPI D0, while its separate GPIO-assignment table lists PA05 for that signal. The LCKFB FPC table also lists PB05, but its GPIO table uses PA05. Neither source explains how the module-pad and connector labels relate. Treat the electrical route as unresolved until you check the schematic/BOM for the exact board revision or verify continuity; do not assume PA05 and PB05 are interchangeable.

## Power Measurement Guidance

For useful ultra-low-power measurements:

- Measure VBAT, VSYS, and VCC_3V3 separately when possible.
- Keep the correct jumper shorted for any rail that is not under measurement.
- Disable avoidable loads such as RGB LED effects, debug logging, display refresh, and sensor polling before measuring sleep current.
- Record board revision, firmware commit, battery or supply voltage, jumper configuration, and sensor state with every measurement.
- Measure both steady sleep current and event current for touch, sensor interrupts, Bluetooth activity, display wake, and vibration events.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD/

Summary: SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD development board: an SF32LB56xV module-based display, audio, storage, and peripheral-development platform.

# SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD

SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD is a display-oriented development board available with either the SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1 or SF32LB56-MOD-A128R12N1 module, both using an SF32LB56xV-series device. Use it to evaluate display interfaces, audio, removable storage, and peripheral drivers before designing a custom SF32LB56x board.

## What It Is Best For

- Display applications using MIPI-DPI (RGB), SPI, DSPI, QSPI, or 8-bit MCU/8080 interfaces.
- Touchscreen integration through I2C.
- Audio experiments with analog microphone input and analog output through the onboard Class-D power amplifier.
- SDIO/TF-card storage and general peripheral-driver development.
- Evaluating an SF32LB56 module-based product architecture before committing to a carrier board.

## Board Resources

<div align="center"><em>Table: SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD Resources</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Resource | Board implementation | Practical use |
|:---------|:---------------------|:--------------|
| N16R12N1 configuration | SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD-N16R12N1 / SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1 | 16 MB QSPI-NOR, 4 MB + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM, and 1 MB QSPI-NOR; module-based evaluation and carrier-board planning. |
| A128R12N1 configuration | SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD-A128R12N1 / SF32LB56-MOD-A128R12N1 | 128 MB QSPI-NAND, 4 MB + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM, and 1 MB QSPI-NOR; module-based evaluation and carrier-board planning. |
| Board size and temperature | 65 mm × 38 mm; -40 °C to 85 °C per the model guide | Mechanical and environmental planning. |
| Display | 24-bit MIPI-DPI RGB through a 40-pin, 0.5 mm FPC connector using the ALIENTEK pin order; SPI/DSPI/QSPI and 8-bit MCU/8080 signals on the 40-pin, 2 × 20 header | Panel bring-up and display-driver development. |
| Touch | I2C touchscreen support | Interactive-display prototypes. |
| Audio | One analog MEMS microphone input and one onboard Class-D PA channel; speaker output up to 3 W / 4 Ω per the model guide | Recording and local playback experiments; check the speaker load and board revision. |
| Storage | MicroSD slot through SDIO | Media, logging, filesystem, and asset tests. |
| USB and power | Two USB Type-C connectors: one USB-to-UART (CH343K per the model guide) and one USB 2.0 FS; either can power the board | Serial logs, download/debug, USB evaluation, and bench power. |
| Power conversion | Onboard 3.3 V and 1.8 V power-conversion ICs | Verify rail requirements against the schematic before adding loads. |
| Debug and boot | 4-pin, 2.54 mm single-row SWD header; Mode boot jumper; power, function, and reset buttons | Firmware download, SWD debug, and boot-mode selection. |
| Indicators | RGB LED, GPIO-controlled LED, and power LED | Firmware and power-state checks. |
| RF | Onboard antenna by default; IPEX selection through a 0 Ω option | Antenna and enclosure evaluation with the module configuration. |

</div>

**Source note — confirm the board revision:** SiFli's detailed board guide identifies the documented board as carrying the `SF32LB56-MOD-A128R12N1` module, with 4 MB + 8 MB co-packaged OPI-PSRAM and 1 Gb QSPI-NAND; it warns that these memory details may change before official release. The current model guide lists both N16R12N1 and A128R12N1, each with 4 + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM and 1 MB standard QSPI-NOR. For A128R12N1, the model guide's 128 MB QSPI-NAND is capacity-equivalent to the detailed guide's 1 Gb. These capacities therefore align for A128R12N1; however, the detailed guide does not mention the 1 MB standard NOR, and it does not establish the SKU fitted to every board or revision. The model guide specifies two USB-to-UART debug channels on the CH343K, while the detailed guide describes the Type-C roles as USB-to-UART and USB 2.0 FS without documenting the channel-to-connector routing. Check the matching schematic/BOM before relying on a particular UART channel. Confirm the module marking and matching schematic/BOM before using a specific unit as a product baseline.

**USB-to-UART bridge discrepancy — verify the fitted part:** The detailed board guide's block diagram labels the bridge CH342K, while the model guide identifies it as CH343K. Verify the actual part against the schematic/BOM for the board revision.

**Photo/prose SKU discrepancy — verify the fitted module:** The detailed guide's prose identifies the documented board as carrying `SF32LB56-MOD-A128R12N1`, but its annotated front-board photo labels the module `SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1`. SiFli does not clarify whether the photo shows another variant or revision. Verify the module marking and board BOM for the unit; do not identify its SKU from the prose or photo alone.

## Programming and Debug

For download mode, install the Mode jumper before powering or resetting the board; remove it for normal application startup and serial-log operation. Connect the host to the USB-to-UART Type-C port with a data-capable cable. The separate USB 2.0 FS Type-C port is available for native USB testing. The board also provides a 4-pin, 2.54 mm single-row SWD header for a compatible debugger. Both Type-C connectors can power the board; follow the board guide and schematic for the intended power arrangement.

## SDK Build Targets

The SiFli SDK uses the following exact board-target names with `scons --board=<board_name>`:

- `sf32lb56-lcd_a128r12n1`
- `sf32lb56-lcd_n16r12n1`

These are SDK build-target identifiers, not necessarily the product names printed on a board or module. The [Supported Boards index](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/supported_boards/index.html) and the SDK's [`build_config_gcc.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-SDK/blob/main/build_config_gcc.yaml) may enumerate different sets; confirm the target against the SDK revision in use.

## First Validation Path

1. Connect a compatible 24-bit MIPI-DPI display to the 40-pin FPC connector, and use the USB-to-UART port with a data-capable USB cable.
2. Follow [Getting Started](../../getting-started/index.md) to establish a known-good build, flash, and serial-log baseline.
3. Bring up solid display patterns before debugging a UI framework; see [Graphics Overview](../../learn/graphics/overview.md).
4. Add touch, storage, audio, or wireless one subsystem at a time, then test coexistence and power behavior.
5. Before a custom design, review [SF32LB56-MOD](../modules/SF32LB56-MOD.md) and [Design for Production](../../hardware/design-for-production.md).

## Reference

SiFli maintains a [development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html) with the selectable board/module codes and a detailed [SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD Development Board User Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/sf32lb56x/SF32LB56-DevKit-LCD.html) with GPIO assignments, header/interface definitions, power notes, and flash/debug procedures.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/devkits/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD/

Summary: SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD: SF32LB58x development board for MIPI DSI, RGB, and QSPI panel bring-up, with audio, SDIO, CAN, and expansion interfaces.

# SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD

## Overview

The SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD is a development board built around the SF32LB58-MOD module family. It supports products using DSI, DPI/RGB, or QSPI displays and provides a practical platform for validating high-resolution UI, audio, storage, USB, and peripheral integration.

The board brings together the SF32LB58x module, multiple display connectors, analog microphone input, stereo speaker output, MicroSD, dual USB Type-C ports, large-core and low-power-core expansion headers, and accessory interfaces such as CAN and SDIO Wi-Fi expansion.

Use the board to validate display, storage, audio, USB, and external peripherals together before committing to a custom design.

## Board and Module Version Notes

<div align="center"><em>Module Version Summary</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Module Version | Basis | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| V1.0.1 | SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 and SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1 using SF32LB586VDD36 | Current version; updates eMMC power control so PA74 controls VCC and PA80 controls VCCQ; adds resistor R0115 |
| V1.0.0 | SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 using SF32LB586VDD36 | Initial module version, as listed in SiFli's module-version section |

</div>

<div align="center"><em>Board Version Summary</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Board Version | Basis | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| V1.0.1 | SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1-V1.0.1 and SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1-V1.0.1 | Current version; adds USB plug detection on PB24; changes the PTC to 2 A / 6 V to support maximum dual-audio output; removes the RGB LED level-shift stage because its timing is unsuitable; replaces the DC/DC converter to reduce output ripple; removes the USB DP pull-up resistor to fix the USB-device interrupt issue |
| V1.0.0 | SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1-V1.0.0 with SF32LB587VEE56 | Initial public board version |

</div>

The SiFli source is inconsistent for V1.0.0: its module-version section identifies SF32LB586VDD36, while its board-version section identifies SF32LB587VEE56 for a board carrying the N16R32N1-V1.0.0 module. Confirm the silicon and module markings on the actual hardware, and check the matching design files before selecting a firmware target or relying on a storage configuration.

## Board Highlights

- SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 or SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1 module, depending on board version
- V1.0.1 uses SF32LB586VDD36 with dual 16 MB HPI-PSRAM and 1 MB in-package QSPI-NOR; the V1.0.0 MCU identifier conflicts in SiFli's source (see the version note above)
- Additional 16 MB QSPI-NOR or 128 MB QSPI-NAND, depending on module variant
- 48 MHz main crystal and 32.768 kHz RTC crystal
- IPEX antenna connector and module RF matching network
- MIPI DSI / RGB888 display support through dedicated FPC connectors
- Dual QSPI / DSPI / SPI display paths exposed through 40-pin headers
- I2C touch-panel support
- On-board analog microphone input and stereo Class-D audio output
- Two USB Type-C ports: one for USB-to-UART download/debug, one for USB 2.0 HS
- MicroSD card slot over SDIO
- Large-core and low-power-core GPIO expansion through two 40-pin headers
- CAN and SDIO Wi-Fi expansion capability

## When to Use This Board

Choose SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD when the project needs a realistic high-end display and peripheral validation platform rather than a minimal breakout board.

- Bring up MIPI DSI, RGB888, or QSPI display panels
- Validate touch, audio, storage, and USB together
- Test high-resolution UI behavior on the SF32LB58x platform
- Evaluate CAN or SDIO Wi-Fi expansion
- Compare NOR and NAND-backed module configurations
- Validate firmware on a flagship-class board before custom PCB work

For module-level integration planning, also review [SF32LB58-MOD](../modules/SF32LB58-MOD.md). For chip-family architecture and display/memory capability, see [SF32LB58x](../chips/SF32LB58x.md).

## Hardware Configuration

<div align="center"><em>Hardware Configuration Summary</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Area | Configuration |
| :--- | :--- |
| Core module | SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 or SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1 |
| MCU by board revision | V1.0.1: SF32LB586VDD36; V1.0.0: SiFli source discrepancy (see version note above) |
| In-package memory (V1.0.1) | 16 MB + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM, plus 1 MB QSPI-NOR |
| Additional storage | 16 MB QSPI-NOR or 128 MB QSPI-NAND, depending on module variant |
| Display | MIPI DSI, DPI/RGB888, and QSPI panel support |
| Audio | On-board analog microphone path plus stereo speaker output |
| USB | USB-to-UART Type-C and USB 2.0 HS Type-C |
| USB-to-UART channels | The SiFli board model guide lists two CH343K USB-to-UART debug channels; the detailed board guide does not map each channel to a specific Type-C connector |
| Storage | MicroSD card slot over SDIO |
| Antenna | Module RF path with IPEX connector |
| Expansion | Two 40-pin headers for large-core and low-power-core expansion |
| Controls and test points | Two user buttons (HOME/long-press reset and function), a separate reset button, MODE boot jumper, and UART/USB/CAN test points |
| Power conversion | On-board DC-DC converters; the SiFli V1.0.1 change log records a converter replacement to reduce output ripple but does not identify the part number. Verify the exact revision in the schematic/BOM. |
| Board dimensions / operating temperature | 65 × 50 mm / −40 to 85 °C |

</div>

## Getting Started

### Required Hardware

- SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD board
- LCD module using MIPI DSI, RGB888, or QSPI, as appropriate
- USB 2.0 data cable, Type-A to Type-C or equivalent
- Host computer running Windows, Linux, or macOS

### Optional Hardware

- Two speakers
- TF / MicroSD card
- J-Link or compatible SWD debugger
- CAN transceiver board
- SDIO Wi-Fi module

### Basic Setup

1. Connect the target display panel to the correct LCD connector.
2. Connect the USB-to-UART Type-C port to the host computer.
3. Open SiFli's download tool and select the correct COM port.
4. Install or remove the Mode jumper depending on whether you want download mode or normal run mode.
5. Power the board and download or run the target firmware.
6. After display bring-up, validate touch, audio, storage, and any expansion peripherals required by the product.

Use a real data-capable USB cable. Some Type-C cables provide power only and will not expose the UART or USB data path.

## Power

SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD is powered from USB Type-C.

- Both on-board USB Type-C connectors can supply power to the board
- For firmware download and UART logging, use the USB-to-UART Type-C port
- Plan the USB 2.0 HS Type-C port separately when validating native USB functions

## Download and Debug

The primary firmware download and serial-log interface is the USB-to-UART Type-C port.

- **Download mode**: install the Mode jumper, then power or reset the board
- **Software debug/log mode**: remove the Mode jumper, then power or reset the board

The board also supports J-Link / SWD debug.

## SDK Build Targets

The SiFli SDK build configuration uses the following exact board-target names with `scons --board=<board_name>`:

- `sf32lb58-lcd_a128r32n1_dsi`
- `sf32lb58-lcd_a128r32n1_qspi`
- `sf32lb58-lcd_n16r32n1_dpi`
- `sf32lb58-lcd_n16r32n1_dsi`
- `sf32lb58-lcd_n16r32n1_qspi`
- `sf32lb58-lcd_n16r64n4`

These are SDK build-target identifiers, not necessarily the product names printed on a board or module. The [Supported Boards index](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/supported_boards/index.html) and the SDK's [`build_config_gcc.yaml`](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-SDK/blob/main/build_config_gcc.yaml) may enumerate different sets; confirm the target against the SDK revision in use. In particular, the index and build configuration do not describe every 58-series target in the same way, and the current [development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html) does not list a matching physical SKU for `sf32lb58-lcd_n16r64n4`.

## Key Module and Expansion Signals

The board exposes both module-level signals and two 40-pin expansion headers. Use the module datasheet and schematic package for the exhaustive pin map; the summary below covers the most design-relevant groups.

<div align="center"><em>Key Functional Signal Groups</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Signal Group | Typical Pins / Signals | Main Use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Download and debug | PB36, PB37, SWDIO, SWCLK, Boot_Mode, RSTN | UART download, software debug, SWD bring-up |
| MicroSD | PA75, PA76, PA77, PA70, PA81, PA79, PB58 | SDIO card interface and card detect |
| RGB LCDC1 | PA12–PA15, PA22–PA27, PA43–PA48, PA50, PA53–PA58, PA61–PA63, PA65, PA67 | RGB888 display path |
| MIPI DSI LCDC1 | DSI_D0–DSI_D3 and DSI_CLK differential pairs | MIPI DSI display path; documented operation supports up to two data lanes |
| QSPI LCDC1 | PA82, PA84, PA86, PA88, PA90, PA91, PA51, PA52 | QSPI display path on the large-core side |
| QSPI LCDC2 | PB02–PB04, PB06, PB08–PB10, PB23, PB27, PB30, PB31, PB34 | QSPI display path on the low-power-core side |
| Touch | PA16, PA17, PA59, PA60, PA92, PA93 | Reset, interrupt, and I2C touch-panel signals |
| Audio | AU_DAC1/2, AU_ADC1/2, MIC_BIAS, PB23 | Analog audio input/output and PA enable |
| CAN / general expansion | PA02, PA11 and header GPIO groups | CAN and peripheral expansion |

</div>

## Display Interfaces

The board supports three main display paths:

- **MIPI DSI** through a 30-pin, 0.5 mm-pitch FPC connector
- **RGB888** through a 40-pin, 0.5 mm-pitch FPC connector compatible with the common ALIENTEK RGB pinout
- **QSPI / DSPI / SPI** through the two 40-pin expansion headers

Supported display guidance from the SiFli source includes:

- MIPI DSI panels up to 2-lane transfer and up to 1280 × 800 resolution
- RGB888 panels up to 1280 × 800 resolution
- QSPI panels up to 512 × 512 resolution

!!! warning "MIPI DSI lane count"
    The board's 30-pin connector pinout labels D0–D3, but the board guide and SDK document operation with up to two data lanes. Do not infer four-lane support from the connector labels. Verify the lane wiring for the exact panel and board revision before use.

![MIPI display wiring reference](assets/sf32lb58x/58KIT-MIPI-J0202.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD — MIPI Display Wiring Reference</em></div>

![LCDC1 QSPI display wiring reference](assets/sf32lb58x/58KIT-LCDC1-QSPI-CONN2.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD — LCDC1 QSPI Display Wiring</em></div>

![LCDC2 QSPI display wiring reference](assets/sf32lb58x/58KIT-LCDC2-QSPI-CONN1.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD — LCDC2 QSPI Display Wiring</em></div>

## Audio

The board supports:

- One on-board microphone input path
- Two audio ADC input paths; resistor jumpers select whether one shared path connects to the on-board microphone or the 40-pin header input
- Two speaker outputs
- One PDM signal path that is multiplexed with RGB signals and therefore unavailable while the RGB display path is active

SiFli's [detailed board guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/sf32lb58x/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD.html) rates stereo analog output at up to 2.8 W/4 Ω, while its [development-board model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/board/devkit_guide.html) lists 3 W/4 Ω for the two speaker outputs. Neither source says whether the rating is per channel or combined. Verify the exact board revision, schematic, and amplifier supply/load conditions before selecting speakers; do not treat either figure as a guaranteed per-channel output.

![Audio wiring reference](assets/sf32lb58x/58KIT-AUDIO-CONN2.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD — Audio Wiring Reference</em></div>

## CAN and SDIO Wi-Fi Expansion

The underlying SF32LB58 module includes a CAN controller, and the board exposes the interface for use with an external transceiver.

![CAN wiring reference](assets/sf32lb58x/58KIT-CAN-CONN1.png){ loading="lazy" }
<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD — CAN Wiring Reference</em></div>
