Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/family/SF32_family/

Summary: SF32LB5xx family overview: heterogeneous Cortex-M33 cores, Bluetooth, ePicasso graphics, and edge AI, with a comparison table and quick chip-selection guide.

# SF32 Family

## Introduction

The **SF32** family, particularly the **SF32LB5xx** series, is a portfolio of highly integrated, ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers developed by SiFli Technologies for battery-powered AIoT and wearable applications.

Designed to fill the gap between traditional microcontrollers and application processors, **SF32** devices combine low-power sensor processing, wireless connectivity, graphics acceleration, multimedia processing, and large-capacity integrated memory in a compact System-in-Package (SiP) architecture. The family is designed for products such as smartwatches, fitness trackers, smart displays, portable medical devices, and connected accessories with edge-processing capabilities.

The **LB** (Low-Power Bluetooth) series is the first SF32 product line. Additional application-focused series are planned.

## Hardware Workflows

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

- :lucide-route:{ .uf-hw-icon .uf-hw-blue } **Plan a Product**

    Follow one path from product requirements and device selection through board validation and production readiness.

    [Plan a Product :material-arrow-right:](product-planning.md){ .uf-hw-link-blue }

- :lucide-list-checks:{ .uf-hw-icon .uf-hw-purple } **SF32 Product Selector**

    Compare SF32 families, select a chip or module, and identify the right development board for early validation.

    [Build a shortlist :material-arrow-right:](../product-selector.md){ .uf-hw-link-purple }

- :lucide-clipboard-check:{ .uf-hw-icon .uf-hw-green } **Design for Production**

    Move from a selected part to schematic, layout, BOM, CAD, checklist, and bring-up evidence.

    [Plan production work :material-arrow-right:](../../hardware/design-for-production.md){ .uf-hw-link-green }

</div>

## Key Features

1. **Heterogeneous Multi-Core Architecture**

    SF32LB microcontrollers employ an Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 based heterogeneous multi-core architecture that balances high-performance application processing with ultra-low-power background operation. Depending on the device, the architecture may include one or more application processors alongside dedicated low-power processors responsible for Bluetooth connectivity, sensor processing, and always-on system functions.

    !!! info "STAR-MC1 Processor"
        STAR-MC1 is a configurable Armv8-M Mainline CPU IP from Arm China, used as the Cortex-M33-class application processor in compatible SF32 devices. Cortex-M33-oriented firmware, middleware, RTOS ports, and tools remain relevant, subject to normal device-specific integration work. Its CU, SP, and SE configurations differ chiefly in cache, TCM, XIPU, and TrustZone capability; Arm Custom Instructions/CDE and the coprocessor interface are optional capabilities. SiFli documentation may use ***Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1*** or ***Arm Cortex-M33*** according to context.

        For device-specific guidance on configuration, TCM, caches, CDE, coprocessors, and representative performance measurement, see [STAR-MC1 Architecture Deep Dive](../../learn/architecture/star-mc1.md).

2. **Ultra-Low-Power Wireless Connectivity**

    The SF32LB series integrates Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) or dual-mode Bluetooth (BT/BLE) connectivity directly on-chip.

    Supported Bluetooth modes and RF performance vary by device. For the exact part number, check the datasheet and validated reference design for supported modes, transmit-power settings, receiver sensitivity, and current consumption; family-level positioning is not a substitute for those figures.

3. **Hardware-Accelerated Graphics and Display Engine**

    All SF32LB microcontrollers integrate ePicasso, a 2.5D graphics engine developed in-house by SiFli, and a separate display controller.

    Hardware acceleration significantly reduces CPU workload for common graphics tasks such as:

    * Alpha blending
    * Image scaling
    * Rotation and transformation
    * Layer composition
    * User interface rendering

    Across the SF32LB family, display interfaces and display types include the following. Availability varies by device; check the exact SKU rather than assuming that every part supports every item listed.

    * SPI / DSPI / QSPI
    * 8080 MCU interface
    * RGB / DPI
    * MIPI DSI
    * EPD
    * JDI (for Memory-in-Pixel displays)

    On devices with the required display interfaces, graphics frameworks such as LVGL can use the hardware acceleration engine to deliver smooth, responsive interfaces on TFT, AMOLED, e-Paper (EPD), and Memory-in-Pixel (MiP) displays.

4. **Edge AI and Neural Acceleration**

    Selected SF32 devices integrate dedicated hardware accelerators for machine learning, multimedia processing, and sensor fusion workloads.

    Capabilities may include:

    * Neural network acceleration
    * Audio processing
    * Voice recognition
    * Camera interfaces (DVP and SPI)
    * Sensor fusion and biometric algorithms

    These features enable low-latency AI inference on-device while minimizing power consumption and cloud dependency.

5. **High-Density System-in-Package (SiP) Memory**

    To support graphics-intensive and AI-enabled applications, SF32 devices integrate instruction and data cache architectures optimized for high-performance execution from external memory.

    Available in-package memories may include:

    * Up to 256 Mb NOR Flash
    * Up to 512 Mb PSRAM

    Only selected part numbers include co-packaged NOR Flash or PSRAM. A SiP configuration can reduce the number of separately mounted memory devices and their associated routing, but memory type, capacity, interface, power, and externally available pins depend on the exact SKU. Check its datasheet and package pinout before finalizing the board.

## SF32 Microcontroller Comparison

<div align="center"><em>SF32 Microcontroller Comparison</em></div>

The values below summarize family-level capabilities, not guaranteed capabilities of every SKU. Interface availability and resource counts can vary by exact part number, package, or configuration; verify the selected part's datasheet.

<div align="center" markdown>

| Feature | SF32LB52x | SF32LB55x | SF32LB56x | SF32LB57x | SF32LB58x |
|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|----------|
| Positioning | Entry-Level | Mainstream with BLE only | Advanced | Enhanced Computing | Flagship |
| Application CPU | Cortex-M33 @240MHz | Cortex-M33 @240MHz | Cortex-M33 @240MHz | 2× Cortex-M33 @240MHz | 2× Cortex-M33 @240MHz |
| Low-Power CPU | Cortex-M33 @24/48 MHz, dedicated Bluetooth controller | Cortex-M33 @48 MHz, user-programmable | Cortex-M33 @48/96 MHz, user-programmable | Cortex-M33 @24 MHz, dedicated Bluetooth controller | Cortex-M33 @48/96 MHz, user-programmable |
| Internal SRAM | 576 KB | 1,312 KB | 960 KB | 592 KB | 3.7 MB |
| Bluetooth | BT Classic + BLE | BLE | BT Classic + BLE | BT Classic + BLE | BT Classic + BLE |
| Graphics Accelerator | 2.5D<br>ePicasso 2.0 Lite | 2.5D<br>ePicasso 1.0 | 2.5D<br>ePicasso 2.0 | 2.5D<br>ePicasso 3.0 + eZip 3.0 | 2.5D + Vector Graphics<br>ePicasso 2.0 + Vivante GCNanoUltraV |
| Display Support | SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / EPD / JDI | SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / JDI / RGB / MIPI | SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / EPD / JDI / RGB | SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / EPD / JDI / RGB | SPI / DSPI / QSPI / 8080 / EPD / JDI / RGB / MIPI |
| Audio ADC | 1x | n/a | 1x | 2x | 2x |
| Audio DAC | 1x | n/a | 1x | 1x | 2x |
| PDM Audio Interfaces | 1x | 1–2x* | 2x | 2x | 2x |
| I²S Audio Interfaces | 1x | 1–2x* | 1x | 2x | 3x |
| USB | 2.0 FS | 2.0 FS | 2.0 FS | 2.0 FS | 2.0 HS |
| CAN | n/a | n/a | 1x | 2x | 2x |
| In-Package PSRAM | Up to 16 MB | Up to 16 MB + 2 MB | Up to 16 MB | Up to 48 MB | Up to 32 MB + 32 MB |
| In-Package NOR Flash | Up to 4 MB | Up to 8 MB | Up to 1 MB | Up to 32 MB | Up to 8 MB |
| # of GPIOs | 44 / 45 | 49 / 95 / 113* | 44 / 120 | 46 / 47 / 58; up to 6 additional BGA112 I/Os* | 154 |
| Package Options | QFN68 | QFN68 / BGA145 / BGA169 | QFN68 / BGA175 | QFN68 / QFN80 / BGA112 | BGA256 |
| Package Footprint (L × W) | 7 × 7 mm | 7 × 7 mm | QFN: 7 × 7 mm<br>BGA: 6.5 × 6.1 mm | QFN68: 7 × 7 mm<br> QFN80: 8 × 8 mm<br>BGA: 5.4 × 4.4 mm | 8.5 × 6.5 mm |
| Power Supply | 3.2–4.7 V (520/3/5/7)<br>2.97–3.63 V (52B/E/G/J)<br>1.8 V (52D) | 1.71–3.63 V | 1.71–3.63 V | 3.0–4.7 V<br>2.97–3.63 V | 1.71–3.63 V |

</div>

**SF32LB55x variant note:** The audio-interface count depends on the order code: SF32LB551/553/555 variants have one PDM and one I²S interface; SF32LB557VD3A6 has two of each. The package summary in the latest [SF32LB55x datasheet (V1.7.2)](https://downloads.sifli.com/user%20manual/DS5501-SF32LB55x-%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E8%A7%84%E6%A0%BC%E4%B9%A6%20V1p7p2.pdf) lists 119 GPIOs for BGA169 (71 HCPU + 48 LCPU), but the same datasheet's detailed product-series table gives 71 HCPU + 42 LCPU = 113 for SF32LB557. The current [SiFli Chip Model Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/silicon/%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.html) also lists 71 + 42 = 113 for SF32LB557VD3A6. SiFli does not explain the discrepancy within the datasheet; this comparison uses the part-specific 113-GPIO figure. Confirm the exact SKU against its datasheet and pin table before assigning pins. Each PDM interface can connect up to two digital microphones; interface count is not microphone count.

**SF32LB55x in-package NOR note:** The 8 MB family maximum includes the separately documented SS6600A8 configuration: two 4 MB QSPI-NOR devices configured as one 8 MB OSPI-NOR device. The SF32-prefixed order codes listed for SF32LB55x have up to 4 MB of in-package NOR Flash; verify the exact model.

**SF32LB57x BGA112 note:** This note applies only to BGA112. SF32LB57x has internal MPI1, MPI2, and MPI3; their positions in a part number are explained in the [SF32 naming convention](SF32_namingrule.md). Under any of these co-packaged-memory configurations, the MPI2 and MPI3 pins are unavailable for external access, leaving a fixed 58 GPIOs: (1) one PSRAM each on internal MPI1 and MPI2; (2) one 256 Mb PSRAM on internal MPI2; or (3) one NOR Flash on internal MPI3. `SF32LB57GVD776` is case (3): the second `7` in its trailing `776` code indicates an internal device on MPI3, so only 58 GPIOs are available. In other BGA112 configurations, the six additional package I/Os may be used for MPI3 or as GP static outputs configured through pull-up or pull-down; they are not unrestricted GPIOs. For example, the `58 + 6` notation for `SF32LB57ZVN7N6` means 58 usable GPIOs plus six pins available for MPI3 or static outputs. QFN68 and QFN80 are outside this BGA112 constraint; they provide only their stated GPIO counts, with no additional MPI3 or static-output option. See the [SF32LB57x product page](../chips/SF32LB57x.md) and its datasheet for the exact SKU.

**SF32LB58x GPIO-count clarification:** The [DS5801 V1.8.3 datasheet](https://downloads.sifli.com/user%20manual/DS5801-SF32LB58x-%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E6%8A%80%E6%9C%AF%E8%A7%84%E6%A0%BC%E4%B9%A6%20V1p8p3.pdf) and SiFli's family comparison specify 154 GPIOs in total (HPSYS: 94; LPSYS: 60). The separate [Chip Model Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/silicon/%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.html) lists HCPU: 94 and LCPU: 66, which sums to 160 and conflicts with the datasheet total. This comparison follows the datasheet; verify usable pins against the exact SKU's package pin table before assigning them.

## Choosing the Right SF32

The SF32LB5xx family spans battery-powered connected devices, from cost-optimized Bluetooth products to systems with advanced graphics and AI features. Family members share an SDK foundation, but processor configuration, peripherals, memory maps, packages, and pin assignments can differ. Porting may require changes to startup code, drivers, linker or partition settings, pin multiplexing, and SDK configuration; validate the result on the target device.

When selecting a device, consider the following key requirements:

* Bluetooth connectivity (BLE or dual-mode BT/BLE)
* Display interface and resolution
* Audio and multimedia capabilities
* Memory capacity
* GPIO requirement
* Graphics performance
* AI and sensor-processing workloads
* Power consumption targets

<div align="center"><em>Quick Selection Guide</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Choose ... | If Your Application Requires ... | Typical Applications |
| : ---      | : ---  | : --- |
| SF32LB52x  | • Dual-mode Bluetooth (BT/BLE)<br> • Integrated audio ADC and DAC<br> • Integrated Li-ion battery charging<br> • Up to 45 GPIOs<br> • Display resolutions up to 512 × 512<br> • A compact and cost-effective solution<br> | • Entry-level smartwatches and fitness bands<br> • Bluetooth modules and wireless adapters<br> • Bluetooth audio accessories<br> • Smart sensors and wearable devices<br> • Electronic shelf labels and smart badges<br> • Portable label printers<br> • eBike and eScooter displays<br> • Basic LVGL-based HMI devices |
| SF32LB55x  | • Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)<br> • MIPI DSI command-mode displays<br>• Large SRAM capacity for sensor processing algorithms<br> • More than 45 GPIOs<br> • Extended low-power processing capabilities | • Fitness bands and activity trackers<br> • Sports and cycling computers<br> • Sensor-rich wearable devices<br> • Health monitoring devices<br> • Battery-powered BLE peripherals |
| SF32LB56x  | • Dual-mode Bluetooth (BT/BLE)<br> • RGB/DPI display interfaces<br> • Integrated audio ADC and DAC<br> • Display resolutions up to 1024 × 600<br> • External Wi-Fi connectivity through SDIO<br> • Increased GPIO capacity | •     Smartwatches with advanced user interfaces<br> • Connected HMI systems<br> • Medical and healthcare devices<br> • Industrial handheld devices<br> • Portable instruments<br> • Advanced eBike and eScooter displays|
| SF32LB57x | • Dual-mode Bluetooth (BT/BLE), BLE Audio, and LE Long Range<br> • ePicasso 3.0/eZip 3.0 graphics with RGB display interfaces<br> • DCMI camera input and integrated high-fidelity audio ADC/DAC<br> • Display resolutions up to 1024 × 600<br> • PTM offload for deterministic I/O or custom peripheral timing<br> • Up to 58 general-purpose GPIOs; where the SiP configuration permits, BGA112 also provides up to 6 I/Os for MPI3 or pull-up/pull-down-configured GP static outputs<br> • SD/SDIO/eMMC storage interfaces | • Compact advanced smartwatches<br> • Display-rich HMI and e-paper devices<br> • Camera-enabled Bluetooth products<br> • Portable audio and recording devices<br> • Smart-home control panels |
| SF32LB58x  | • Dual-mode Bluetooth (BT/BLE)<br> • Advanced graphics rendering including vector graphics<br> • MIPI DSI command-mode or video-mode displays<br> • Display resolutions up to 1280 × 800<br> • Large memory configurations<br> • High GPIO density and count<br> • External Wi-Fi connectivity through SDIO<br> • Edge AI and machine-learning workloads | • Premium smartwatches<br> • Sports and outdoor wearable devices<br>• Advanced cycling computers<br> • Smart displays and connected dashboards<br> • AI-enabled wearable devices<br> • Edge AI and sensor-fusion systems|

</div>

## Software Compatibility Across the Family

The SF32 platform provides a shared software and SDK foundation. However, processor configuration, peripherals, memory maps, packages, and pin assignments can differ. Porting may require adapting startup code, drivers, linker or partition settings, pin multiplexing, and SDK configuration, followed by validation on the target hardware.

Evaluate software reuse and migration effort alongside performance, memory, display, and connectivity requirements. Do not assume that devices in the same family are pin-compatible or that firmware will run unchanged.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Which SF32 chip suits a low-cost Bluetooth smartwatch or fitness band?**
SF32LB52x is the entry-level choice: dual-mode Bluetooth (BT Classic + BLE), integrated audio ADC/DAC and Li-ion charging, up to 45 GPIOs, and a 7 × 7 mm QFN68 package.

**Which SF32 chips support Classic Bluetooth, not just BLE?**
SF32LB52x, SF32LB56x, SF32LB57x and SF32LB58x support BT Classic + BLE. SF32LB55x is BLE only.

**Which SF32 chips support MIPI DSI displays?**
SF32LB55x and SF32LB58x list MIPI display support. SF32LB52x, 56x and 57x use SPI, QSPI, 8080, JDI/EPD and (56x/57x) RGB interfaces instead.

**Which SF32 chips offer camera input or CAN?**
SF32LB57x adds DCMI camera input. CAN is available on SF32LB56x (1×) and on SF32LB57x and SF32LB58x (2×).

**Are SF32 family members pin-compatible?**
No. They share an SDK foundation, but cores, peripherals, memory maps, packages and pin assignments differ, so porting needs driver, pin-mux and configuration changes and must be validated on the target device.

Source: https://uForge.io/sf32-products/family/SF32_namingrule/

Summary: How to decode an SF32LB5xyZxYx6 part number: product tier, PSRAM variant, package type, integrated Flash/PSRAM capacity, and temperature grade, with worked examples.

# SF32 Naming Convention

## Chip Naming

### Part Number: ***SF32LB5xyZxYx6***

!!! note "Syntax Note"
    * Lowercase ***x*** denotes a numeric digit.
    * Uppercase ***Y*** or ***Z*** denotes an alphabetic character.

### Prefix: *SF32LB5xy*

- **SF32** — SiFli 32-bit MCU Series
- **LB** — Product Line Identifier
    - **LB**: Low-power Bluetooth MCU series
- **5** — Processor Family
    - **5**: Devices based on a 32-bit Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 processor, or a RISC-V processor with comparable performance
- **x** — Product Tier
    - **8 / 7**: Two application processors and one low-power processor; product positioning varies by family.
    - **6 / 5**: Mid-range (***single*** application processor, ***single*** low-power processor)
    - **2**: Cost-optimized (***single*** application processor, ***dedicated*** low-power Bluetooth controller)
- **y** — Device Variant
    - Its value generally reflects the in-package PSRAM capacity; the exact mapping varies by product sub-family.

### Suffix: *ZxYx6*
- **Z** — Package Type
    - **U**: QFN68
    - **V**: BGA
    - **Y**: QFN80
- **xYx** — Integrated Memory Configuration (QSPI-NOR Flash & PSRAM)
  *(Note: Exact encoding mapping depends on the specific package and device family)*

Treat `ZxYx6` as a family-level pattern, not a fixed-width parsing template. The number and order of memory codes vary by device family and package: a numeric Flash code may be absent, and a PSRAM letter may repeat when multiple devices are integrated. Decode each exact order code against its family-specific variant table.
<div align="center"><em>Part Number Suffix Field Definitions</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Field | Type | Options | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **x** | Numeric | **1** to **6** | Generic QSPI-NOR Flash capacity mapping:<br>• **1**: 2 Mb<br>• **2**: 4 Mb<br>• **3**: 8 Mb<br>• **4**: 16 Mb<br>• **5**: 32 Mb<br>• **6**: 64 Mb<br>SF32LB57x also uses codes **7** and **8**; see its family-specific map below. |
| **Y** | Alphabetic | **A** to **E** | Integrated PSRAM capacity & interface:<br>• **A**: 16 Mb QPI-PSRAM<br>• **B**: 32 Mb OPI-PSRAM<br>• **C**: 64 Mb OPI-PSRAM<br>• **D**: 128 Mb OPI/HPI-PSRAM<br>• **E**: 256 Mb HPI-PSRAM |

</div>

- **6** — Operating Temperature Grade
    - **5**: −20°C to +70°C (Commercial)
    - **6**: −40°C to +85°C (Industrial)

### SF32LB57x-Specific Memory Codes

The SF32LB57x part-numbering figure in the [hardware design guide](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB57x_hardware_design_guide.md#33-packages) shows three memory-position codes after the package code, in MPI1, MPI2, and MPI3 order; the temperature-grade code follows them. The family-specific codes for each MPI position are:

<div align="center"><em>Table: SF32LB57x Memory Codes by MPI Position</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Code | SF32LB57x meaning at the corresponding MPI position |
|:-----|:----------------------------------------------------|
| `N` | No co-packaged memory |
| `B` | 32 Mb PSRAM |
| `C` | 64 Mb PSRAM |
| `D` | 128 Mb PSRAM |
| `E` | 256 Mb PSRAM |
| `2` | 4 Mb NOR Flash |
| `3` | 8 Mb NOR Flash |
| `4` | 16 Mb NOR Flash |
| `5` | 32 Mb NOR Flash |
| `6` | 64 Mb NOR Flash |
| `7` | 128 Mb NOR Flash |
| `8` | 256 Mb NOR Flash |

</div>

This map is specific to SF32LB57x. Confirm each complete code against the exact variant table; the map does not imply that every combination is an orderable SKU.

### Part Number Examples

#### Example 1: SF32LB527UD6
**SF32LB52 Series** cost-optimized MCU configuration:

* **Processor Configuration:** Single application processor and a dedicated low-power Bluetooth controller processor (Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 based).
* **Package Type:** QFN68 package (**U**).
* **Memory Configuration:** Integrated 128 Mb OPI-PSRAM (**D**).
* **Operating Temperature:** −40°C to +85°C (**6**, Industrial Grade).

#### Example 2: SF32LB587VEE56
**SF32LB58 Series** flagship MCU configuration:

* **Processor Configuration:** Dual application processors and one low-power processor (Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 based).
* **Package Type:** BGA256 package (**V**).
* **Memory Configuration:** Integrated dual (2x) 256 Mb HPI-PSRAM (**E**) and one 32 Mb QSPI-NOR Flash (**5**).
* **Operating Temperature:** −40°C to +85°C (**6**, Industrial Grade).

#### Example 3: SF32LB57GVD776

The SF32LB57x variant table lists this as a BGA112 part. Its three memory-position codes are `D/7/7`: MPI1 has 128 Mb PSRAM, MPI2 has 128 Mb NOR Flash, and MPI3 has 128 Mb NOR Flash. The final `6` is the industrial temperature grade. The second `7` in `776` therefore identifies the MPI3 NOR Flash; see the [SF32 family overview](SF32_family.md) for the BGA112 GPIO implication.

#### Example 4: SF32LB57ZVN7N6

The SF32LB57x variant table lists this as a BGA112 part. Its memory-position codes are `N/7/N`: no co-packaged memory on MPI1, 128 Mb NOR Flash on MPI2, and no co-packaged memory on MPI3. The final `6` is the industrial temperature grade. The family overview explains why its `58 + 6` entry does not mean 64 unrestricted GPIOs.

### 55x Legacy Suffix Exceptions

The SF32LB55x family was defined before the current naming pattern, so some order codes retain legacy suffix layouts. These three order codes do not decode fully from the `SF32LB5xyZxYx6` pattern above: `SF32LB551U4O5`, `SF32LB555V4O6`, and `SF32LB555V436`. Confirm their package and memory configuration in the exact 55x variant table and datasheet rather than inferring fields from the generic pattern. `SF32LB557VD3A6` follows the current naming convention and is not a legacy exception.

## Module Naming

### Part Number: ***SF32LB5x-MOD-y-AaaaBbbbCccc***

!!! note "Syntax Note"
    * In the generic suffix, `A`, `B`, and `C` identify the three storage-field positions; they are not literal characters in every module name.
    * The first character within each populated field identifies the storage type. The remaining digits identify its capacity or configuration.
    * The `-y` subtype field is currently used only by the SF32LB52 module family. Published SF32LB56-MOD and SF32LB58-MOD names are not using it.

### Prefix: *SF32LB5x-MOD-y*

- **SF32LB5x** — Module MCU family
    - **SF32**, **LB**, and **5** follow the same series, product-line, and processor-family meanings as the chip naming convention above.
    - **x** identifies the product tier: **8 / 7** has two application processors and one low-power processor, with positioning varying by family; **6 / 5** is mid-range; **2** is cost-optimized.
- **MOD** — SiFli module product.
- **y** — Module subtype, when the family defines one
    - **1**: Direct Li-ion battery operation for SF32LB520/3/5/7 devices. The chip supply range is 3.2–4.7 V; the standard configuration uses SF32LB525UC6 with 8 MB OPI-PSRAM.
    - **A**: Regular 3.3 V operation for the SF32LB52B family. It does not support direct Li-ion battery supply; the chip supply range is 2.97–3.63 V. The standard configuration uses SF32LB52BU36 with integrated 1 MB QSPI-NOR Flash.
    - **B**: Regular 3.3 V operation for the 52E/52G/52J family. It does not support direct Li-ion battery supply; the chip supply range is 2.97–3.63 V. The standard configuration uses SF32LB52EUB6 with integrated 4 MB OPI-PSRAM.

The `-A` module has no external NOR Flash fitted. It can connect to an external NOR Flash or SDIO peripherals, including Wi-Fi, SD-NAND, and eMMC in 4-bit mode.

### Suffix: *AaaaBbbbCccc*

<div align="center"><em>Module Part Number Suffix Field Definitions</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Field | Storage-type code | Capacity, configuration, and suffix |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `Aaaa`<br>Variable Flash | `N`: QSPI-NOR Flash<br>`A`: NAND Flash (interface depends on module family)<br>`D`: SD-NAND Flash<br>`E`: eMMC | `N16`: 16 MB QSPI-NOR Flash<br>`A128`: 128 MB SPI-NAND on SF32LB52-MOD-1; 128 MB QSPI-NAND on SF32LB56-MOD and SF32LB58-MOD<br>`D128`: 128 MB SD-NAND on SF32LB56-MOD<br>`E4`: 4 GB eMMC on SF32LB58-MOD |
| `Bbbb`<br>PSRAM | `R`: PSRAM | `R4`: 4 MB OPI-PSRAM<br>`R8`: 8 MB OPI-PSRAM<br>`R12`: 4 MB + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM<br>`R16`: 16 MB OPI/HPI-PSRAM<br>`R32`: 16 MB + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM<br>`R64`: 32 MB + 32 MB HPI-PSRAM |
| `Cccc`<br>Standard Flash | `N`: QSPI-NOR Flash | `N1`: 1 MB QSPI-NOR Flash<br>`N4`: 4 MB QSPI-NOR Flash |

</div>

The three suffix fields are concatenated without separators. `Aaaa` is the variable Flash option, `Bbbb` is the PSRAM option, and `Cccc` is the standard Flash option. The source guide defines the listed type-and-capacity combinations; do not assume that every type code can be combined with every capacity code. A field appears only when the documented module configuration uses it.

### Part Number Examples

#### Example 1: SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8

**SF32LB52 lithium-battery module configuration:**

* **Module Subtype:** `-1` supports direct Li-ion battery operation with a 3.2–4.7 V chip supply.
* **Variable Flash:** `N16` indicates 16 MB QSPI-NOR Flash.
* **PSRAM:** `R8` indicates 8 MB OPI-PSRAM.

#### Example 2: SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1

**SF32LB58 flagship module configuration:**

* **Module Subtype:** No `-y` subtype is used for published SF32LB58-MOD names.
* **Variable Flash:** `A128` indicates 128 MB QSPI-NAND Flash for this SF32LB58-MOD configuration.
* **PSRAM:** `R32` indicates 16 MB + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM.
* **Standard Flash:** `N1` indicates 1 MB QSPI-NOR Flash.

The naming pattern describes a configuration, not a guarantee that every code combination is a released SKU. The SiFli guide identifies SF32LB566VCB36 and SF32LB586VDD36 as standard MCU configurations for the SF32LB56-MOD and SF32LB58-MOD families respectively; additional module configurations may be customized. Confirm availability, fitted MCU, pinout, and electrical specifications in the applicable module documentation.

[SiFli Chip Model Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/silicon/%E8%8A%AF%E7%89%87%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.html) · [SiFli Module Model Guide](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-Wiki/blob/main/source/zh_CN/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.md)

# Plan a Product

This guide maps the decisions needed to take an SF32 concept from initial requirements through validation to a production-ready design plan. Follow the stages in order while the chip, module, development board, software stack, and manufacturing approach are still undecided.

## Product Planning Path

<div align="center"><em>Table: SF32 Product Planning Path</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Stage | Key decision | Start here | Exit criterion |
|:------|:-------------|:-----------|:---------------|
| 1. Define requirements | Wireless device role, display, audio, AI, storage, power supply and consumption budget, package area, and target product lifetime. | [SF32 Family](SF32_family.md) | A ranked shortlist with explicit must-have interfaces and constraints. |
| 2. Select integration | A custom PCB with the chip mounted directly, a module plus carrier board, or a development board for early validation. | [SF32 Product Selector](../product-selector.md) | A preferred device and integration approach, plus the closest available board or module. |
| 3. Prove the software baseline | Toolchain, flash flow, serial output, and one known-good example on the selected or closest board. | [Getting Started](../../getting-started/index.md) | A repeatable build-and-flash process with a captured console log. |
| 4. Validate product risks | Product-specific behavior of the display, Bluetooth, audio, AI, and storage, plus the power-supply path and consumption profile. | [Tutorials](../../getting-started/tutorials/overview.md), [Learn](../../learn/index.md), and [Develop](../../develop/index.md) | Measured results for the subsystems that drive cost, power, or schedule risk. |
| 5. Freeze the implementation plan | Schematic, layout, memory/partition plan, BOM, test approach, update/recovery behavior, and manufacturing assumptions. | [Design for Production](../../hardware/design-for-production.md) | Reviewed design package and an explicit list of remaining validation items. |

</div>

## Do Not Skip the Board Validation Loop

A family comparison and a successful compile are not enough to select a production device. Validate the closest board before freezing hardware, then record the board name, SDK version, SDK example used, measured behavior, and differences from the intended product. If the final product uses a new display, storage part, battery path, antenna, or module carrier, treat each as a separate validation item.

For a complete worked path, choose the closest [Reference Design](../../hardware/reference-designs/reference-designs.md) after the initial hardware and software baseline is established.

## Handoff Checklist

- [ ] The selected part or module meets the product's interface, memory, package, power-supply, and power-consumption constraints.
- [ ] A supported board or deliberate custom-hardware validation plan exists.
- [ ] The software path and its maturity are accepted by the product team.
- [ ] Recovery, OTA/DFU, logging, and factory-programming needs are defined before partition and BOM decisions are frozen.
- [ ] The correct hardware design guide, checklist, AVL, and EDA library have been identified.

The SF32 Products section helps you move from a product idea to an implementable SF32 design. Use it to understand the SF32 family, make and verify a hardware choice, find a reusable baseline, and reach the design material needed for production.

## Choose Your Starting Point

## What This Section Covers

Start with the [SF32 Family Overview](family/SF32_family.md) when you need to understand the available families and the broad capability differences between them. The [naming rules](family/SF32_namingrule.md) help decode a complete part number once you have narrowed the family and package.

Use the [SF32 Product Selector](product-selector.md) when requirements such as power architecture, package, display, audio, memory, GPIO, connectivity, or specialist hardware determine the choice. It establishes a shortlist; the exact part number, package, electrical limits, and board-level routing must still be confirmed against the relevant SiFli documentation.

Once a direction is selected, continue through the [reference designs](../hardware/reference-designs/reference-designs.md) and [production path](../hardware/design-for-production.md). This is where the site connects a device choice to reference hardware, design guidance, CAD libraries, BOM decisions, review checklists, and bring-up evidence.

Already know the kind of hardware you need? Go straight to the relevant catalogue:

- [Chips](family/SF32_family.md) for device-family and part-selection information.

Hardware documentation defines the physical product path. For SDK setup, examples, toolchains, and software-platform support, continue to [Develop](../develop/index.md).

Summary: SF32LB52-MOD-1: low-power Bluetooth 5.3 MCU module family for SF32LB52x, with integrated RF circuitry, a 48 MHz crystal, and SKU-dependent antenna options.

# SF32LB52-MOD-1

## Overview

SF32LB52-MOD-1 is a low-power Bluetooth MCU module family built on the SF32LB52x platform. The standard N16R8 SKU uses SF32LB525UC6. The 27.9 × 18.0 × 3.1 mm module combines the dual-core Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 platform, RF circuitry, a 48 MHz crystal, and an antenna connection. Depending on the part number, it uses either an on-board PCB antenna or an IPEX connector for an external antenna.

DS5203 V0.3 documents an on-module PCB antenna and says an IPEX-connected external antenna is available on another model, but does not map antenna options to the published memory-SKU list. Confirm the exact antenna configuration with SiFli before finalizing the carrier-board layout. The finished product still requires RF validation and applicable product-level certification. The exposed interfaces provide the Bluetooth, graphics, and audio functions used in compact connected products.

Depending on the selected SKU, the chip package may include OPI-PSRAM. The module interface exposes key functions of the underlying chip family, including GPIO, SPI, LCD, MPI, UART, I2C, PWM, SDIO, USB 2.0 FS, and analog audio.

!!! info
    For the underlying chip family, architecture, and peripheral set, see [SF32LB52x](../chips/SF32LB52x.md). This page focuses on module-level integration, power, package, and variant selection.

## Applications

**SF32LB52-MOD-1 is recommended for** products that need Bluetooth, graphics, and audio capability with lower RF and layout risk, including:

- Smartwatches, fitness bands, and wearable medical products
- Bluetooth sensor hubs and connected accessories
- Smart locks, smart-home devices, and compact appliances
- Small graphical HMI products
- Vehicle key fobs and wearable remote products
- Cost-sensitive connected display devices

Consider SF32LB52-MOD-1 when the product needs one or more of these capabilities:

- Module-level RF integration with PCB-antenna and external-antenna options
- Exposed interfaces for the chip platform's Bluetooth, graphics, and audio capabilities
- Reuse of SF32LB52x software and peripheral capability
- Compact module integration for space-constrained wearable or HMI products

## Features and Specifications

### Compute and Memory

- Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 application core (HCPU), up to 240 MHz, up to 370 DMIPS / 984 EEMBC CoreMark
- 32 KB instruction cache and 16 KB data cache
- 512 KB retention SRAM
- Dedicated ultra-low-power Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 core (LCPU), up to 24 MHz, with 64 KB retention SRAM
- Single-precision FPU and MPU on both cores
- Optional in-package OPI-PSRAM depending on module SKU

### Wireless Connectivity

- Dual-mode Bluetooth 5.3 with BLE Audio support
- Sensitivity: -100 dBm (BLE/1 Mbps), -96.3 dBm (BR), -95.5 dBm (EDR2)
- Maximum transmit power: 19 dBm (BR/BLE), 13 dBm (EDR2/EDR3)
- BR peak receive current: 2.4 mA @ 3.8 V

### Graphics and Display

- ePicasso 2.0 2D/2.5D graphics engine
- eZip 2.0 lossless graphics decompression accelerator
- LCD controller supporting 8080, SPI, Dual-SPI, and Quad-SPI interfaces
- Practical fit for compact watch-style or small-HMI display products

### Audio

- 1 × 24-bit audio DAC
- 1 × 24-bit Sigma-Delta audio ADC
- 1 × I2S interface
- 1 × PDM interface
- Analog audio input/output support exposed through the module interface

The PDM interface can connect up to two digital microphones; the number of PDM interfaces is not the microphone count. Actual connectivity depends on pin multiplexing and board routing. On this module, PA22/PA23 are unavailable externally when the optional 32.768 kHz crystal is populated; the hardware guide documents an alternate PDM pin mapping.

### Storage Interfaces

- Optional in-package OPI-PSRAM, depending on module SKU
- 1 × MPI (QSPI) for external SPI NOR or SPI NAND
- 1 × SD/SDIO supporting SD3.0, SDIO3.0, and eMMC

### Security

- AES, HASH, and CRC hardware accelerators
- True random number generator (TRNG)
- PSA Certified Level 1

### Power, Package, and I/O

- Module package: 27.9 × 18.0 × 3.1 mm
- Operating temperature: -40 to 85 °C
- VSYS: 3.2–4.7 V for direct Li-ion battery input, or 3.7–4.7 V from a regulated supply; 3.8 V is recommended.
- IO voltage: 3.3 V
- VBATS: 0–4.7 V battery-sense input that can also be used for ADC measurement. Connect the voltage to be measured directly; do not use an external resistor divider.
- VDD33_VOUT2: on-module 3.3 V LDO output for external peripherals. It is off by default and must be enabled in software; maximum output current is 150 mA, and total capacitance on the rail must not exceed 7.4 µF.
- 68-pin module interface; signal pins expose multiplexed functions including GPIO, SPI, LCD, MPI, UART, I2C, PWM, SDIO, USB 2.0 FS, and digital and analog audio

## Module Variants

<div align="center"><em>SF32LB52-MOD-1 Module Variants</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Module Code | Chip | Flash | PSRAM | Temperature | Dimensions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB52-MOD-1-N16R8 | SF32LB525UC6 | 16 MB QSPI-NOR | 8 MB OPI-PSRAM | -40 to 85 °C | 27.9 × 18.0 × 3.1 mm |
| SF32LB52-MOD-1-A128R16 | SF32LB527UD6 | 128 MB SPI-NAND | 16 MB OPI-PSRAM | -40 to 85 °C | 27.9 × 18.0 × 3.1 mm |

</div>

The [SiFli module-model guide](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-Wiki/blob/main/source/en/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.md) and EPD application guide also list A128R16, but the linked DS5203 V0.3 datasheet lists only N16R8. Confirm current availability and memory configuration with SiFli before selecting A128R16.

The A128R16 Flash labels differ across the official sources: the [OpenSiFli module-model guide](https://github.com/OpenSiFli/SiFli-Wiki/blob/main/source/en/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.md) identifies 128 MB SPI-NAND, while SiFli's [board-model guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/board/devkit_guide.html) lists 128 MB QSPI-NAND for the corresponding DevKit SKU. The sources do not explain whether this reflects the fitted part or interface wording. Confirm the Flash part and bus mode against the schematic/BOM for the exact board revision before using the board configuration as a module baseline.

### Chip

### Development Kits

The [SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD](../devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-LCD.md), [SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3](../devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Core-3p3.md), [SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano](../devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-Nano.md), and [SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP](../devkits/SF32LB52-DevKit-ULP.md) are practical starting points for firmware validation before moving to a custom module carrier design.

Typical end products include entry-to-mid-tier smartwatches, fitness bands, Bluetooth sensor hubs, smart locks, and compact graphical HMI devices.

Summary: SF32LB56-MOD: general-purpose low-power Bluetooth 5.3 MCU module family based on SF32LB56xV, with 4 MB + 8 MB of co-packaged OPI-PSRAM and SKU-dependent Flash variants.

# SF32LB56-MOD

## Overview

SF32LB56-MOD is SiFli's general-purpose, low-power Bluetooth MCU module family based on the SF32LB56xV platform. The standard configuration uses an SF32LB566VCB36 with 4 MB + 8 MB of co-packaged OPI-PSRAM and 1 MB of QSPI-NOR. The module combines dual-core MCU processing, Bluetooth 5.3 with BLE Audio support, graphics acceleration, audio interfaces, SKU-dependent Flash variants, and an integrated RF path in a compact form factor.

The module integrates the RF path, crystal, and high-speed memory, and supports either an on-module PCB antenna or an external antenna connected through an IPEX-compatible connector. Validate RF performance in the finished product, and design the carrier board around the selected antenna arrangement. The module's interfaces and memory configurations support products with display, audio, sensing, and local-processing requirements.

The family is available in multiple memory configurations. All variants measure 18.0 × 32.9 × 3.1 mm and are rated for operation from -40 to 85 °C. The [SF32LB56-MOD hardware design guide](../../hardware/chip-guides/SF32LB56-MOD_hardware_design_guide.md), based on DS5602 V0.3, provides further antenna and layout details. The SiFli module-model guide lists the memory configurations but does not map antenna options to SKUs. Confirm the antenna arrangement of the selected module with SiFli before finalizing the carrier-board layout.

!!! info
    The compute, graphics, and audio features below describe the SF32LB56xV platform integrated in the module; external availability depends on the module pinout and pin multiplexing. For the chip family's architecture and full peripheral set, see [SF32LB56x](../chips/SF32LB56x.md). This page focuses on module integration, SKU-dependent memory, power rails, and product fit.

## Applications

SiFli lists the following application areas for SF32LB56-MOD:

- Wearables: high-end smartwatches, smart bands, wearable medical devices, and fitness equipment
- Industrial: cost-effective display solutions, graphical HMI, industrial sensor-control centers, equipment monitoring, and instruments
- Automotive: electric-vehicle central-control devices, car keys, and wearable vehicle remotes
- Home automation: small and medium-sized smart appliances and smart locks
- General: low-power sensor hubs and Bluetooth Mesh
- AIoT examples: voice-command recognition, smart-home devices, smart keys, and smart control panels

Consider SF32LB56-MOD when the design needs one or more of these capabilities:

- Module-level integration of the RF path, antenna option, crystal, and high-speed memory
- Memory configuration choices across the listed module SKUs
- Interfaces for display, audio, sensing, and local processing
- Compact module dimensions for space-constrained products

## Features and Specifications

### Compute and Memory

- HCPU: Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1, up to 240 MHz, up to 370 DMIPS / 984 EEMBC CoreMark
- LCPU: Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1, up to 96 MHz, up to 148 DMIPS / 394 EEMBC CoreMark
- HCPU memory system: 32 KB instruction cache, 16 KB data cache, and 800 KB SRAM, including 128 KB retention SRAM
- LCPU memory system: 16 KB instruction cache, 8 KB data cache, and 160 KB retention SRAM
- Single-precision FPU and MPU on both cores
- Neural-network matrix accelerator and signal-processing accelerators for richer local workloads

### Wireless Connectivity

- Dual-mode Bluetooth 5.3 with BLE Audio support
- Sensitivity: -100 dBm BLE 1 Mbps, -96.3 dBm BR, -95.5 dBm EDR2, -88.5 dBm EDR3
- Maximum transmit power: 19 dBm for BR/BLE, 13 dBm for EDR2/EDR3
- BR peak receive current: 2.2 mA at 3.3 V

### Graphics and Display

- ePicasso 2.0 2D/2.5D graphics engine
- Hardware rotation, scaling, mirroring, and alpha blending
- Graphics workloads up to 1024 × 1024
- eZip 2.0 lossless graphics decompression and eZip-A animation support
- LCD support for 8080, SPI, Dual-SPI, Quad-SPI, DPI/RGB, and JDI
- TurboPixel: extDMA compresses the final framebuffer using fixed-ratio lossy compression, and the display controller decompresses it. This reduces the PSRAM bandwidth and framebuffer capacity required by a given workload.

### Audio

- 1 × 24-bit audio DAC
- 1 × 24-bit Sigma-Delta audio ADC
- 2 × PDM interfaces (PDM1/PDM2), each supporting left/right microphone channels
- 1 × I2S interface
- Audio sample-rate conversion and EQ acceleration

Each PDM interface can serve up to two digital microphones, so the two interfaces can support up to four microphones in total. PDM interface count is not microphone count; actual connectivity depends on pin multiplexing and board routing.

### Memory and Module Variants

<div align="center"><em>SF32LB56-MOD Memory Configurations</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Module Code | Flash by SKU | PSRAM | Standard Flash | Temperature | Dimensions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB56-MOD-N16R12N1 | 16 MB QSPI-NOR | 4 + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 18.0 × 32.9 × 3.1 mm |
| SF32LB56-MOD-A128R12N1 | 128 MB QSPI-NAND | 4 + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 18.0 × 32.9 × 3.1 mm |
| SF32LB56-MOD-D128R12N1 | 128 MB SD-NAND | 4 + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 18.0 × 32.9 × 3.1 mm |

</div>

The [SiFli Module Model Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.html) lists these three configurations and notes that other configurations can be customized. Confirm current SKU availability and memory configuration with SiFli.

SiFli identifies SF32LB566VCB36 with 4 MB + 8 MB OPI-PSRAM and 1 MB QSPI-NOR as the standard configuration; this matches the N16R12N1 memory configuration. The model guide does not assign a chip part number to A128R12N1 or D128R12N1 individually; confirm the exact chip part number for either SKU with SiFli.

### Power and I/O

- VDD_3V3 recommended operating range: 2.97–3.6 V
- VDD_1V8 recommended operating range: 1.7–1.95 V
- VDDIO recommended operating range: 1.7–3.6 V
- VDD_3V3, VDD_1V8, and VDDIO must power up together
- PA00–PA11 interface level is fixed at 3.3 V and does not follow VDDIO
- 89-pin module interface
- Operating temperature: -40 to 85 °C

### Chip

Built on [SF32LB56x](../chips/SF32LB56x.md), specifically the SF32LB56xV platform family. Use the chip page for the broader architecture, display, audio, and package context behind the module.

### Reference Products

SiFli's documented application areas include wearables, industrial display and HMI equipment, vehicle-control products, smart-home appliances, low-power sensor hubs, and Bluetooth Mesh products.

Summary: SF32LB58-MOD: low-power Bluetooth MCU module based on SF32LB586VDD36, with standard 16 + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM, 1 MB QSPI-NOR, and NOR, NAND, or eMMC storage variants.

# SF32LB58-MOD

## Overview

SF32LB58-MOD is a low-power Bluetooth MCU module based on SiFli's SF32LB586VDD36. The standard configuration includes 16 + 16 MB of HPI-PSRAM and 1 MB of QSPI-NOR. The 24 × 24 × 3.1 mm module combines the triple-core platform, RF path, crystal, and memory options with external interfaces for display, audio, storage, and control.

The module integrates the BGA256 device, RF path, crystal, and high-speed memory within the module, reducing the amount of related routing on the product carrier board. The finished product still requires RF validation and applicable regulatory approvals. Confirm the antenna option and memory configuration for the selected SKU before finalizing the carrier-board design.

Depending on the selected module SKU, the platform can combine HPI-PSRAM with QSPI-NOR, QSPI-NAND, or eMMC storage. The module's interfaces support products that need display, audio, storage, and connectivity capabilities while retaining an MCU-class platform.

DS5802 V0.1 identifies an on-module PCB antenna and external-antenna configurations. An external antenna may connect through castellated pads or the first-generation external antenna connector, which is compatible with Hirose U.FL, I-PEX MHFI, and Amphenol AMC connectors. The datasheet does not map these options to individual SKUs, so confirm the antenna implementation of the selected module with SiFli before finalizing the carrier-board layout.

!!! info
    For the underlying chip family, architecture, and peripheral set, see [SF32LB58x](../chips/SF32LB58x.md). This page focuses on module-specific integration, memory variants, power rails, and product-fit decisions.

## Applications

SiFli lists the following application areas for SF32LB58-MOD:

- Wearables: high-end smartwatches, smart bands, wearable medical devices, and fitness equipment
- Industrial: cost-effective display solutions, graphical HMI, industrial sensor-control centers, equipment monitoring, and instruments
- Automotive: electric-vehicle central-control devices, car keys, and wearable remote controls for vehicles
- Home automation: small and medium-sized smart appliances and smart locks
- General: low-power sensor hubs and Bluetooth Mesh
- AIoT examples: voice-command recognition, smart-home devices, smart keys, and smart control panels

Consider SF32LB58-MOD when the design needs one or more of these capabilities:

- Module-level integration of the BGA256 device, RF path, crystal, and high-speed memory
- On-module PCB antenna or external antenna routed through castellated pads or a connector compatible with Hirose U.FL, I-PEX MHFI, and Amphenol AMC connectors; confirm the SKU configuration
- Memory choices spanning QSPI-NOR, QSPI-NAND, and eMMC configurations
- External interfaces for display, audio, storage, and control

## Features and Specifications

### Compute and Memory

- 2 × Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 application cores, up to 240 MHz
- 1 × user-programmable Arm Cortex-M33 STAR-MC1 low-power core, up to 96 MHz
- Up to 370 DMIPS / 984 EEMBC CoreMark per application core
- Up to 148 DMIPS / 394 EEMBC CoreMark on the low-power core
- 2176 KB SRAM (HCPU) + 512 KB SRAM (ACPU) + 1056 KB retention SRAM (LCPU)
- Single-precision FPU and MPU on all cores

### Wireless Connectivity

- Dual-mode Bluetooth 5.3 with BLE Audio support
- Sensitivity down to -107.5 dBm for BLE Long Range at 125 kbps
- Maximum transmit power: 19 dBm (BR/BLE), 13 dBm (EDR2/EDR3)
- BR/EDR2/EDR3 peak receive current: 2.2 mA @ 3.3 V

### Graphics, Display, and Multimedia

- ePicasso 2.0 2D/2.5D graphics engine
- Vivante GCNanoUltraV vector graphics engine
- Hardware JPEG codec
- Dual LCD controllers supporting 8080, SPI, Dual-SPI, Quad-SPI, DPI/RGB, MIPI DSI, and JDI
- TurboPixel: extDMA compresses the final framebuffer using fixed-ratio lossy compression, and the display controller decompresses it. This reduces the PSRAM bandwidth and framebuffer capacity required by a given workload.
- Always-on-display support on both LCD controllers

### Audio

- 2 × 24-bit audio DACs
- 2 × 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADCs
- 2 × PDM interfaces (PDM1/PDM2)
- 3 × I2S interfaces, all in master mode; I2S1 is input-only, while I2S2 and I2S3 support input and output
- Analog audio input/output support exposed through the module interface

The [SF32LB58x hardware design guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/hardware/SF32LB58x-HW-Application.html) lists two PDM microphone inputs (PDM1 and PDM2). A single PDM interface can carry two microphone channels: SiFli's [PDM SDK example](https://docs.sifli.com/projects/sdk/latest/en/sf32lb52x/example/multimedia/audio/4pdm/README.html) demonstrates two-microphone capture on the left and right channels of one interface, or four-microphone capture across PDM1 and PDM2. However, the example does not list SF32LB58-MOD as a supported platform. For this module, verify the intended microphone/channel configuration in the target SDK and check pin multiplexing and carrier-board routing; do not infer four-microphone support from the two-interface count alone.

### Storage Interfaces and Module Variants

<div align="center"><em>SF32LB58-MOD Module Variants</em></div>

<div align="center" markdown>

| Module Code | Selectable Storage | PSRAM | Standard Flash | Temperature | Dimensions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| SF32LB58-MOD-N16R32N1 | 16 MB QSPI-NOR | 16 + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 24 × 24 × 3.1 mm |
| SF32LB58-MOD-A128R32N1 | 128 MB QSPI-NAND | 16 + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 24 × 24 × 3.1 mm |
| SF32LB58-MOD-E4R32N1 | 4 GB eMMC | 16 + 16 MB HPI-PSRAM | 1 MB QSPI-NOR | -40 to 85 °C | 24 × 24 × 3.1 mm |

</div>

The [SiFli Module Model Guide](https://wiki.sifli.com/en/silicon/%E6%A8%A1%E7%BB%84%E5%9E%8B%E5%8F%B7%E6%8C%87%E5%8D%97.html) lists these variants, notes that eMMC may be included as an internal device, and states that other configurations can be customized. Select a SKU based on the required storage medium and capacity, then confirm availability and memory configuration with SiFli. Also verify that the selected device and boot/storage path are supported by the target SDK and firmware.

### Power, Package, and I/O

- Module package: 24 × 24 × 3.1 mm
- Operating temperature: -40 to 85 °C
- VDD_3V3: 2.97–3.6 V
- VDD_1V8: 1.7–1.95 V
- VDDIOA / VDDIOA2 / VDDIOB: 1.7–3.6 V
- VDD_3V3 supplies AVDD33_ANA, AVDD33_AUD, and AVDD_USB; when eMMC is fitted, it also supplies the eMMC VDD input. SiFli recommends an LDO for this rail.
- VDD_1V8 supplies PVDD1, PVDD2, AVDD_BRF, and AVDD18_DSI, as well as the co-packaged memory.
- VDDIOA supplies PA I/O except PA00–PA11, the external Flash, and eMMC VIO when eMMC is fitted. VDDIOA2 supplies PA00–PA11; VDDIOB supplies PB I/O.
- 138-pin module interface; multiplexed pins expose functions including GPIO, SPI, LCD, MPI, UART, I2C, PWM, SDIO, USB 2.0 HS, and audio

## Related Products

### Chip

Built on [SF32LB58x](../chips/SF32LB58x.md). Use the chip page for the broader graphics, memory, and display architecture behind the module.

### Development Kits

The [SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD](../devkits/SF32LB58-DevKit-LCD.md) board is a practical starting point for firmware validation, display bring-up, and audio/storage-path checks before moving to a custom carrier design around the module.

### Reference Products

SiFli's documented application areas include wearables, industrial display and HMI equipment, vehicle-control products, smart-home appliances, low-power sensor hubs, and Bluetooth Mesh products.
